map.h2terror:2.event.0.description:
The Black Mark, a smelly little hole of a tavern, was loud and dimly lit. Bidley sat in the corner sipping cheap beer. He had grown to hate this place more than anything, but couldn't bring himself to break his old tradition.

The door opened, and a man clad in a garish jacket walked in. He bore a striking resemblance to Bidley, though shorter and slighter, and he was followed by a gorgeously dressed, attractive woman. The man approached Bidley and shouted merrily, “Aha, you old dog! Long time no see! Where have you been?”
Bidley rose and hugged his brother.
“You haven't changed a bit—the same young drunkard I used to know. What's going on?”
“Ah, nothing much,” Jeremy said with a wave of his hand as he sat down next to his female companion. “By the way, this is Casmetra, the High Hydromancer.”
“Bidley, Captain Bidley,” he replied.
“A pleasure to meet you, Captain. I've heard plenty about you,” said Casmetra.
“Oh, indeed? And what have you been told so far?” grinned Bidley, taking a sip of his foul drink.
“I heard that you saved Xanthor, Catherine's archmage.”
Jeremy gave a whistle. “Shiver my soul! Working for Erathians, brother?” 
“How could I possibly have known I'd find Xanthor in that cell?” grumbled Bidley. “He was a waste of time, on top of being a bastard and an ingrate. Now there's a rumor going around that I work for the queen! ‘Her Majesty's corsair...'”
“Ingrate, huh?” Casmetra asked in surprise.
“Well, not completely. He told me a legend about something called the Horn of the Abyss...”
“Impossible!” exclaimed the sorceress, and both pirates gave her a surprised look.
“What's so special about it?” asked Jeremy.
“Have you ever heard of Armageddon's Blade, or the Cloak of the Undead King?” Casmetra asked excitedly. “These are legendary artifacts, of exceptional power! Completely unique! The Horn of the Abyss is another one like that. It is said that it lies on the bottom of the sea somewhere, ready for taking. One who finds it will rule the seas—he'll become the living representation of the Water Lord!”
“Interesting,” Bidley murmured. “Xanthor told me exactly where the Horn is. If it wasn't a lie, of course.”
“You can't imagine the importance of this knowledge,” whispered Casmetra, pressing one elegant hand to her cheek.
“Well, then, let's go find that Horn of the Abyss!” exclaimed Jeremy.
“No, it's way too risky: we don't have enough men, ships, or supplies. We're just two captains with a handful of sea dogs on board,” Jeremy's brother replied.
“You also have me, the High Hydromancer, and my apprentices,” added Casmetra. “And I know how to get everything we need. We'll have to put some effort into it, though.” 
“By the way, Jeremy,” Bidley suddenly changed the topic. “I heard you've run into some trouble. How is the Black Unicorn doing?”

“It sank,” Jeremy replied, leaning back in his chair.
map.h2terror:2.event.1.description:
“Eeofol's shore,” Bidley commented, contemplating the land from the wall of the new fort. Far ahead, he could see the shimmering heat and smoke rising from the ashy black terrain, like a festering boil on Antagarich's body. Somewhere over there swarmed legions of terrible creatures; they marched across the scorched earth toward the lands of men.
“Those beasts have plenty of everything,” said Casmetra.
“They're too preoccupied with their war against Erathia and its allies to notice us. We'll be able to gather the riches we need to afford the Cornucopia.”
“Excuse me, what?” asked Jeremy. 
“The Cornucopia,” repeated the sorceress. “We'll have to hire craftsmen to make the necessary elements of the artifact, and then we'll use the Cornucopia to hire an army and prepare our fleet. However, this artifact has one flaw: it depletes itself over time and eventually breaks. Nobody can say for sure for how long it will serve us.”
“How do you know all this about the Cornucopia?” Bidley asked.
“They say Archibald Ironfist had such an artifact. It supplied his armies during the Succession wars in Enroth. One of the reasons for his defeat was that the Cornucopia stopped working,” Casmetra replied.
“By the deep, woman,” grinned Jeremy, “where did you learn all that about Archibald? I thought you'd been sitting on that rock in the sea your whole life.”
“Never you mind that,” Casmetra answered grimly. “Gentlemen, we have matters to attend to.”
map.h2terror:2.event.2.description: Scouts report an Erathian outpost to the south: Carstrig Fort. It would be good to capture it and use for our needs. The fort's defenders wouldn't have a chance against the Kreegans anyway.
map.h2terror:2.event.3.description:
A group of frightened crewmen rushed into the room. “Cap'n! Giant crocodile-men just walked ashore!”
Without hesitation, Bidley grabbed his sabre and ran to see it for himself.
Indeed, two great scaly creatures, not unlike lizardmen, were lying on the shore, breathing heavily.
“Shiver me timbers!” exclaimed Bidley as he knelt beside them. “What are these creatures?”
“Those are nix,” Casmetra announced, approaching from behind. “An ancient sea-dwelling race of intelligent reptiles. They were thought extinct. Long ago, their kingdom was somewhere around here. Something must have made them emerge from heir depths again. I'm sure we'll see more of them.”
“I hope they have good intentions,” Bidley replied.
map.h2terror:2.event.4.description: More nix arrived with each passing day. It turned out that many of them could speak and even wield weapons. They explained that their ancient city was on a rocky island nearby, and that it was besieged by demons. When their prince, Tark, tried to break the siege, he was imprisoned. Tark is being held hostage in a Kreegan prison somewhere near Eeofol's shore. Bidley has decided to save him: the nix may become valuable allies.
map.h2terror:2.event.5.description:
Casmetra called a meeting between herself, Bidley, and Jeremy. 
“I bear grim news. My sources report that the Kreegans think Catherine hired the pirates to flank and backstab their forces, so they're moving some of their rearguard forces to the seashore. They'll soon attempt to kick us out of here. The faster we assemble the Cornucopia, the better,” she informed them. 
“Blood and thunder! That'll do wonders for my reputation,” muttered Bidley dispiritedly. “Every damn sea dog will think I'm working for Erathia, as if saving that mage wasn't enough.”
“But isn't that a good thing, brother?” asked Jeremy. “Discounts at taverns! Free entrance to the kingdom's largest ports! The only thing I'm worried about is how to find enough money to pay these artifact-making swindlers.” 
“We can slaughter the Kreegans and pillage them. We are pirates, after all!” exclaimed Bidley, and Jeremy agreed with a grin. 
“Call up the boys! We're gonna be turning fire demons into sea demons soon.”
map.h2terror:2.event.6.description:
I was in the hold having a bout with a bottle of rum, and one of us was certainly about to win, when Patris appeared.
“Cap'n, I'd like to talk to you about what's going on,” he said.
“All right, I'm listening,” I nodded.
“I don't like that this woman is dragging you into this trouble. Why are you risking your neck going after that artifact? We're losing good men fighting those demons,” my first mate said seriously.
“It was our own decision,” I replied. “No one was dragging us into it. The life of an honorable pirate is one of constant risk—you know that. And by the way, we'll have a new ship soon, a beautiful one—a frigate! All those bigmouths in Regna will bite their tongues.” 
“All right, Cap'n. You're the boss,” agreed Patris and left me to my own devices. Wish I knew why he disliked Casmetra so much.

map.h2terror:3.event.0.description:
As Tark watched the pirates load their army and resources onto their ships, he couldn't help but be preoccupied about his people. They had managed to keep their existence a secret from the rest of the world for ages, but many of them were either dead or imprisoned now.
“Tark, will you follow us, or do you have other plans? We are grateful for your help and help of your people...” Bidley started.
“It is I who should be grateful,” Tark interrupted. “You showed me that there is life beyond my princedom. The only thing left to do is to set my people free. I know where they are,” the reptile leader continued.
“Perhaps we could help?” Bidley offered.
“No. You have one path ahead of you, and I have another. I must save my people. Don't assume that all the nix you meet will know of you or help you, however. There are just as many scoundrels among the nix as among men,” replied Tark, turning toward the sea.
“Will we meet again?” asked Bidley.
“Probably,” the nix replied. “If I return, I'll come find you. If not... forget about me.” With that, Tark strode into the water until it reached his waist, then dove and disappeared.
map.h2terror:3.event.1.description:
Tark swam for a long time, but at length, he reached the subterranean kingdom of the warlock lords. A small colony of nix, independent from the island princedom where Tark ruled, had lived in these underwater caverns until the warlocks conquered and enslaved them. It was time to free those nix, and also to show them who their true ruler was. Tark was the last of an ancient line of nix princes. Something terrible had happened to their race: as a result of some mysterious disease, many of their eggs were turning out to be hollow and devoid of life. As a result, their population had slowly dwindled, and the once flourishing people had been reduced to a mere handful of nix, controlling one small island and its surrounding waters. 
Though to the casual eye he seemed like a slow-moving and slow-thinking reptile, Tark absorbed information quickly. He knew that the lords of Nighon were in the throes of a civil war right now. Were he to invade their lands and take over one of their towns, they would hardly pay attention right away.
map.h2terror:3.event.2.description: Tark knew he wouldn't be able to save everyone, but perhaps he could help the majority get out. Those he is unable to rescue will have to flee and fend for themselves if they want to live. After interrogating the civilians of his newly-occupied town, Tark learned that the lords were busy fighting and wouldn't notice the loss of this city for a while. Moreover, Tark found out that the captured nix were working in the caverns one level below. The fetid vapors those tunnels were full of were deadly to minotaurs, humans, and troglodytes, but hardly affected the nix. The warlocks particularly prized their nix slaves for this trait.
map.h2terror:3.event.3.description: It's dark and stuffy in these caves. Tark has decided to find a new, better home for his people. Perhaps those pirates, widely-traveled as they are, will know of a quiet place to settle—somewhere the nix can put down roots and slowly restore their civilization without fear of invaders. For this reason, Tark has decided to join Bidley and his followers as soon as he has freed his enslaved kin.
map.h2terror:3.event.4.description: Sooner or later, these lords will end their squabble and take notice of their lost outpost. It's important to be ready for their coming and to prepare a counterstrike they will be unable to recover from.
map.h2terror:3.guards.66.65.0.message:
“I can't believe my eyes! You are one of noble kin!”
“I am Prince Tark.”
“I bow before thee, prince. I escaped the poisonous mines on the lower level. When the Nighon war started, they loosened their grip over the slaves. But why did you come, Prince Tark?” 
“My duty is to free as many of our kin as possible.”
“Then allow me to join you. I am a seasoned warrior, and I have this armor I took from a slain minotaur. I am ready to give my life to aid our people,” said the warrior, and knelt.

map.h2terror:4.event.0.description:
Indeed, it was a good idea to make proper preparations before going for the Horn. The pirates' path ran south of Tatalia, toward a group of unknown islands. Either it was a coincidence, or somebody had been spying on them, but they ran into Tatalia's royal fleet in their way: two frigates and nearly a dozen smaller vessels. The smaller ships were easy to sink, but as soon as frigates approached it was clear that they had to withdraw. Bidley's caravel gave one last volley and, propelled by a tailwind, began flanking the dangerous waters. Jeremy was right behind, followed by the galleys. However, the Tatalian frigates pursued, trying to rip their sails in hopes of stopping the daring pirates. One of the enemy ships caught up and pounced upon their galleys. Lizardmen with daggers clenched in their teeth leapt into the water and climbed on board to head for the sails, turning the deck into a bloodbath.
Eventually only one galley was left: the one under Patris' command. This was the first time he had taken charge of a vessel as a captain. 
“We must stop the Tatalians immediately,” said a determined Casmetra. “With magic.”
“Won't you hit Patris' galley?” Jeremy asked in alarm.
“I don't know. What happens happens,” answered the sorceress.
“Wait! We cannot risk his life!” Jeremy cried.
Casmetra wasn't listening. With an elegant gesture, she wove a destructive spell that summoned icebergs from the water. They grew rapidly, destroying everything in their way. Chunks of ice and wood rained down on the pirates' fleet. The Tatalian frigate took bad damage, and a galley got ripped apart, impaled on a rising spike of ice.
Once the mayhem was over, Casmetra retired to her cabin. Jeremy stood frozen for a while, looking at the now-receding monstrous iceberg that had saved his life, taking his friend's as it did. He had always known that sooner or later he would lose his first mate and his other close friends. That's the risk of being a pirate. But he didn't expect it to happen today.
map.h2terror:4.event.1.description:
With heavy losses of ship and crew, Bidley's crippled fleet arrived at the location marked by Xanthor. It was an inconspicuous little island encircled by craggy mountains. The words “Island of the Vengeful Serpent” had been scribbled by an unknown traveler's hand onto one of the stones sticking out of the water.
“I don't see any Horn here,” observed Jeremy.
“Of course not, my friend! The Horn is inside the Serpent's maze, deep underground. And only I know how to get there!” announced Casmetra, and after taking a step forward she spread her hands wide and began to cast a spell.
The sorceress' words turned into blazing signs and letters that flew toward the mountain, before getting swallowed by it. When she finally went silent, the mountains let out a roar and a voice like the clanging of hammer on anvil sounded:
“Password approved. Opening the passage.”
“What was that?” asked a startled Bidley.
“I don't know,” shrugged Casmetra. “They say that the Oracle of Enroth sounds sort of like that.”
“A thousand devils! This is... indescribable!” exclaimed Jeremy.

An ominous black passage opened between the mountains. A stone ladder was visible inside, its other end lost in the darkness. Bidley armed himself: a pistol in one hand and a sabre in the other.
“We have to be extremely cautious,” warned the sorceress. “There are plenty of traps and illusions below.”

Bidley nodded, and, taking lead of a band of trusty sea dogs, he began a descent into the darkness. Just as Jeremy and Casmetra were about to follow him, the iron-like voice boomed:
“Second level of protection negated. Terminating access.”

The last pirate was just about to turn around and jump out, but the mountains sealed back up right before his nose. Jeremy frantically punched and kicked at the mountain face, but nothing could open the passage again. Casmetra tried her spell once more, but this time it didn't work.

“Damnation! I lost my first mate and my brother at once!” shouted Jeremy, cutting a palm tree down with his sabre in his rage.
“Calm down! Your brother is alive. He is inside the maze now. Whether he gets out or not depends on him!” said Casmetra, resting her hand on Jeremy's shoulder.
“Oh, that's just great. And what do you plan to do now?” asked Jeremy vexedly, without turning around. 
“Return to camp and wait for Bidley. I'm sure he'll be all right.”
map.h2terror:4.event.2.description:
Bidley ended up in a series of damp caves with his small group of men. Strangely enough, the place was not as dark as it had looked at first; the caverns were lit by an odd bluish glow.
“Where to, Cap'n?” one of the sea dogs asked. 
“Onward,” answered Bidley. “We're leaving this place with the Horn, or we ain't leaving it at all. I trust that fate hasn't given up on us.”
map.h2terror:4.event.3.description:
Casmetra was gazing into a magical globe. Jeremy, seeing this, walked around her to try to get a look. 
“Careful! You'll turn into a frog!” said the priestess.
“Seriously?” Jeremy exclaimed, jumping backwards. 
“No, just joking. But the frogs are still around.”
“What?” the pirate asked in confusion.
“Tatalians,” explained Casmetra. “Their fleet has retreated, but they're repairing their ships. Their warriors are on the shore, recuperating. Soon they'll muster the courage to track us down again, and they'll try to destroy us. They probably think Regna has decided to raid Tatalia.” 
“We have to hold them back somehow,” said Jeremy. “Otherwise, Bidley will get out, only to meet the grinning mugs of those frogs. And dogs.”
map.h2terror:4.event.4.description:
I summoned my courage to call Casmetra into my cabin. The sorceress entered, her gown swishing softly, and gave me an inquisitive look. I looked her straight in the eye. “Casmetra, I have this suspicion that you could have cast that spell without hitting Patris' galley.” 
“What makes you think that?” Casmetra inquired, looking surprised. “Such spells are not easy to control. They're like your cannon: you can't be sure exactly where the all will fly, can you? But when it does hit something, it does damage.”
“I can hit a flying bird!” I flew into a fit of rage. “And don't you patronize me... Patris was there! I noticed the conflict between you and him,” I insisted.
“What? Do you honestly believe that I would doom my own apprentices and a crew of excellent fighters just because of one grumpy old man?” Casmetra stamped her foot on the ground, eyes flashing. 
“I... I'm sorry, I hadn't thought about that,” I muttered in reply and plopped down on my bunk, totally confused. “It's just... I keep going over and over this. Patris sleeps with the fishes. My brother is stuck in the underworld, and gods only know whether he'll make it out of there alive. I've been getting plastered every night just to get some sleep.”
Casmetra smiled softly, and approached me. “You are tired, Jeremy. You need to take a break,” she said, caressing me with her slender hands. I must admit, her fragrance was most pleasing. 
“Indeed… Break is good,” I smiled.
map.h2terror:4.event.5.description: I have been thinking about Patris and his home on that far-off island—that home he'll never return to. It's possible someone survived that sinking, but the chances are pretty slim. One day I will visit that archipelago, and find Patris' wife and daughter—or avenge them, if the local governor is a cur who harms the innocent. We pirates always carry out the last wish of the dead.
map.h2terror:4.guards.100.25.1.message:
A diary page, yet again.
“...mpossible! This damnable place! Sandra turned into a monster right in front of me. I don't know what it was—an illusion or a real curse—but I had to slay her, or whatever it was she had become. I've lost most of my people. Oh gods, I have never been so miserable or so clueless!”
map.h2terror:4.guards.49.28.1.message:
Another page from the diary.
“...nt here. The scariest part is that the labyrinth is full of crazed people who've been roaming here for who knows how long. That's in addition to the water beasts and other cursed creatures. It's madness how many brave men have perished here. Will I end up among them? The task isn't easy. Mistress has warned me about the traps and illusions I'll face...”
map.h2terror:4.guards.69.36.1.message: Another page from the diary: “This is the end. Almost everyone is dead. I barely escaped with my life! Those terrible giant serpents... I have never seen such creatures. This time it wasn't an illusion. This is what my mistress warned me about. Somebody's upon my heels, and I doubt he wants to ask for directions to the local library. I must prepare myself for battle—probably my last. Soon, no one will remember the humble mage Da....”
map.h2terror:4.guards.77.92.1.message:
Bidley found an abandoned raft with some remnants of food and some pieces of parchment that look to be a page from somebody's journal.
“…od footwear. So I had to wrap my legs with linen rags. Mistress said this labyrinth is full of treasures, on top of the Horn itself. So with any luck, I'll find some magical boots for myself. However, I'm leaning toward the thought that...”
How interesting! Somebody was here before, also searching for the Horn of the Abyss. Did he succeed? Bidley took the page and continued his journey.
map.h2terror:4.guards.85.61.1.message:
Bidley found another parchment page floating on the water.
“...last! Panic overwhelms me in this dungeon. I haven't the slightest clue what to do or where to go. I hope this whole idea pays off. I am goi....”
map.h2terror:4.guards.86.5.1.message: “There is your Horn, in that box. Grab it, quick!” said Dargem impatiently.
map.h2terror:4.guards.9.12.1.message:
Bidley approached the collapsed tunnel. A feeble, shaky voice came through the rubble: “Hey, buddy! I hear you walking there, and you don't sound like some shambling dead! Help me! Get me out”
“I'm not your buddy, guy,” answered Bidley calmly. “First, tell me who you are, and what you're doing here.”
“My name is Dargem. I'm just a mage who was in the wrong place at the wrong time. Can't deal with these rocks on my own.” 
“Aren't those your scribblings that I've been finding scattered around all the way here?” asked the pirate. 
“My diary? And I was wondering where it went! I was caught in a trap here,” the prisoner replied.
“Were you after the Horn of the Abyss?” Bidley demanded.
“Yes. And so are you, I assume—no one comes here for the fresh air.”
“And why would I let a competitor out?”
“Wait!” begged Dargem. “Don't go! I'm no competitor to you! I don't need the Horn, not anymore! Take it for yourself, and do whatever you want with it! Blow it, drink rum from it, stick it down your... I don't care. But without me you won't be able to get past the illusions.”
“What illusions?” Bidley asked alarmedly, stepping closer to the rubble. 
“Some of the sea serpents you'll see aren't real. But you won't be able to tell the real ones from the fake ones without the magical spell I have,” explained the prisoner.
“All right. You've just about convinced me.”

map.h2terror:5.event.0.description:
Everything happened so quickly. Water bubbled up, and a massive geyser emerged from the sea, spitting out a magical vessel. Casmetra said that Bidley was on that ship, in the company of someone else who had captured both my brother and the Horn.
“It's Dargem,” said priestess angrily.
“And what's a Dargem?” 
“A mercenary mage. Worked for Regna—or, to be precise, for one of Regna's lords. It's a nest of vipers there, everyone trying to stab everyone else in the back. One of those lords wanted to get his hands on the Horn of the Abyss, and his desire was stronger than yours. So he sent Dargem.” 
“Blast that... we have to chase them down, immediately! Diego, prepare the ships!” I ordered.

We chased Dargem awhile, but eventually hi ship disappeared from sight behind an island. Instead of him, we were welcomed by Regna's fleet. We had only a handful of ships ot our own disposal, so we had to flee. We set up camp on a small island and decided to muster forces for a strike on Dargem's fortress, where he is holding the Horn and my brother. I hope Bidley is safe.  
However, we have some good news: Tark has returned! He emerged from the water with his kin, just outside our camp.
“I promised to return,” hissed the giant reptile leader laconically.
“We have trouble. Bidley was captured,” I explained. 
“We nix will fight for you. Some will be against you, however. But I am the prince, and my cause is just,” replied Tark.
map.h2terror:5.event.1.description:
“Jeremy,” smiled Casmetra. “I bring more good news. The theft of the Horn awakened the sea serpents. Now they are wandering the ocean.” 
“That's great news—at least we'll be having plenty of smoked eel, I guess.”
“Silly,” Casmetra replied. “These creatures still feel they have to protect the Horn of the Abyss. And yet, the poor stupid things can't figure out whether it has to be returned, or guarded wherever it is. I can enchant them so that the serpents who want to return the Horn will help us fight to get it back from that traitor Dargem.”
“That's a good idea,” I agreed. “But what will we tell them once we get the Horn from Dargem? ‘As you were, we were just kidding?'”
“You men always try to think twenty steps ahead,” Casmetra groaned, rolling her eyes. 
But for all that, I certainly wasn't going to turn down an offer of help from the sea serpents. Even one of those beautiful creatures could sink a frigate!
map.h2terror:5.event.2.description: Scouts report that the Tatalians, angered by their recent defeat, are hoping to get their entire fleet wiped out yet again. They found us on this archipelago, previously known only to pirates. They've raised a fort somewhere to the east, and are preparing for an invasion. On the one hand, this could be great; they're not likely to be able to tell the difference between two pirate bands. On the other hand, it won't be pretty if they, and not us, capture Dargem. If that happens, Bidley will surely hang on a rope right beside that scoundrel.
map.h2terror:5.event.3.description: More troubling news: war has broken out again between Erathia and Eeofol. Also, odd towns with golden-domed castles have begun appearing out of thin air all across the continent. Casmetra thinks it is an invasion by elemental lords. One of these towns sprang up in the northern region of the archipelago. They've probably been attracted by the power of the Horn of the Abyss and hope to acquire it.
map.h2terror:5.event.4.description:
I got tired of this pointless resistance and decided to write Dargem a letter. My mind wasn't perfectly clear at the time; invigorated by rum, I wrote the following: 
“Dargem! This is Jeremy Albatross, Admiral of Regna's armada. You have crossed my path and captured my brother. Set him free immediately, and yield the artifact to us! If you do, I promise that you and your men will be allowed to leave the island unharmed.”
map.h2terror:5.event.5.description: Tark's nix report that there is a massive network of caves under this archipelago. Many of them are filled with water, but some parts are dry. The caves are ancient; something unique and powerful might be found inside.
map.h2terror:5.event.6.description:
Dargem surely took his time in writing me back. I imagine that is just one more demonstration of his stupidity and inability to think critically—a trait I famously possess. His letter went as follows:
“My esteemed self-styled Admiral Jenny Grouse! I spent far too long in those caves waiting for Lady Luck to smile on me and send me a traveler even less fortunate than myself. And so it happened. I deserve the Horn—though I haven't figured out how it works yet. I suggest you get lost. Your brother is merely a guarantee of my security. As soon as you are gone, he shall be freed. Dargem”
map.h2terror:5.event.7.description:
I've been thinking about what Dargem said. I called Casmetra in my cabin and told her that I was thinking about retreating, to ensure Bidley's safe release. The priestess's eyes widened.
“Jeremy! How could you even think something like that!” she exclaimed.
“But we could save Bidley, and avoid unnecessary bloodshed,” I began, when Casmetra interrupted me.
“You can't even imagine what a villain Dargem is, and what is at stake here. The Horn of the Abyss is one of the greatest artifacts ever created. There's no record of who made it—it was probably created before the Silence. It is a gift from the Age of Wonders! If only we can figure out how it works, we will be equal to gods!” the priestess explained with excitement. She stepped up to the table and, to my amusement, took a hearty gulp of my rum. “Dargem is a scoundrel and a monster. The only reason he hasn't already killed Bidley is that we're close by. If you leave, he'll have your brother murdered and fed to the sharks. You should realize that. Unless you're a coward...” she suggested with reproach in her eyes.
“No, milady. Jeremy Albatross is the bravest and boldest of all the pirates between Enroth, Antagarich and Jadame!” I declared, jumping to my feet.
“And that's why I love you,” laughed the priestess, embracing me.
map.h2terror:5.event.8.description: Dargem's raiders attacked our supply ships and vanished into the night.
map.h2terror:5.event.9.description:
- It's halyava time!
- No, AI, no!!!
map.h2terror:5.guards.0.140.0.message: Are you ready to dispense justice?
map.h2terror:5.guards.111.20.1.message: Will you dare take this ancient volume?
map.h2terror:5.guards.113.8.1.message: Terrible frost and grim silence affect your crew negatively.
map.h2terror:5.guards.114.3.1.message: These caves are as ancient as the world...
map.h2terror:5.guards.130.59.1.message: There is a whole nest of sea serpents here!
map.h2terror:5.guards.133.26.1.message: It looks like there is a secret passage here.
map.h2terror:5.guards.60.136.1.message: Bear in mind that this monolith may lead anywhere, and it will not be easy to get back.
map.h2terror:5.header.description: Jeremy, Tark, and Casmetra must capture Dargem. The mission will be lost if Jeremy is defeated. This is the last mission in the campaign.
map.h2terror:5.header.name: Treachery
map.h2terror:5.monster.117.26.1.message: Your presence here has not gone unnoticed. A powerful creature has awakened...
map.h2terror:5.monster.128.4.1.message: The guardians of the ancient palaces are on the alert!
map.h2terror:5.quest.30.11.0.firstVisit: A group of pirates displeased with Dargem's leadership would like to join you.
map.h2terror:5.quest.9.21.0.firstVisit: A group of pirates displeased with Dargem's leadership would like to join you.
map.h3horn:0.event.1.description:
I almost feel like all this has already happened to me before. Once again, I'm marooned on a beach, once again I'm shipless... only Patris is no longer around. Anyway, the last thing I remember is getting sucked into some kind of crater, just as that harlot Kasmetra grabbed the damn Horn. That vile witch! An anchor up her bunghole! She was never into me, or anything! She only wanted the Horn of the Abyss! A thousand drowned souls! Alright, just you wait now... No one has yet escaped the wrath of Jeremy Albatross!
I also lost my boot. Again.
Somewhere not far behind loitered a handful of lads that had gotten sucked in with me. Were the rest less lucky, I wonder? I sure hope not. We still had to something to help Bidley... "Hey ya rapscals!" I shouted to the men. "We've got to get out of here... but first we need to figure out where we are... a shark up my gullet."
map.h3horn:0.event.10.description: Timur's men report of a vast cave network beneath the isles. Both monsters and intelligent beings dwell there. I don't have high hopes about those "intelligent" beings far surpassing our regular "abrrghs", however. Should we go searching for the Grail down there?
map.h3horn:0.event.11.description:
Alarming news have reached me: the caves are teeming with abrrghs AND demons. Damn it, maybe even Tuunbaq himself, for good measure. During the First War, the Kreegans had sent an expedition here. However, Catherine was able to vanquish the forces of Eeofol and Nighon before the expedition could arrive. The alliance with Eeofol was broken, and the Kreegans were left abandoned in these caves. I doubt they have gotten any nicer over the time.

Just my luck. Can a man get marooned devil knows where, lose a boot and NOT meet Kreegans in the end?
map.h3horn:0.event.2.description:
Yet again I have a feeling that I relive past events, with an exception of me being on some shallow stinky island. My Utopia is likely thousands of miles away from here. Quite frankly, I have a feeling that we are somewhere a Kreegan has never set its hoof. Even the air feels different here... And we have to find a settlement right away to replenish our water supplies. 

This is the merriest part of a sea wolf's life: a chance to die of dehydration while surrounded by water. But Jeremy Albatross knows better than to be afraid of such petty threats! I am more inclined to think that perils and hardships build a pirate's character. Once my biography comes out of print, it will certainly say that I was the most courageous and noble of all pirates!
map.h3horn:0.event.3.description:
A short, swarthy, cross-eyed man with thin, rat-like mustache was standing before me. I think I heard of folks like that, leading nomadic lives somewhere in Krewlod. I figured out he was probably a leader here. 
"And who might you be?" I asked, squinting. "Name's Timur," He answered.
"And who are your people? What are you doing here?"
"No, who are you?" Exclaimed Timur. "We lived here peacefully, never making any trouble, before you came, killing everyone and destroying the fort!" 
"Answer the question!" I bellowed.
"We are refugees. I used to work on the plantations," answered the local man. 
"What plantations?" I inquired.
"There's a big island to the north," answered my swarthy new acquaintance. "New Steadwick town is there." 

That was when I understood where I was, and the revelation did not make me happy.
"New Steadwick!" I screamed, making Timur cower in fear, along with my own men. "New Steadwick! You rat-face... Tell me it's a joke!" I grabbed him by the collar and put my sabre to his throat.
"I swear on my blood and honor!" he wailed, sweating bullets. "It is called that for real!" 
"Hear that, men?" I let poor Timur go and turned to my crew while gesturing profusely, "Sink me! You do realize where we are, right?!"
map.h3horn:0.event.4.description:
Very far away, east of Erathia, lies an archipelago amongst endless ocean. We pirates call it the Gilbert Isles. Erathians call it Klondike. Some time ago, during Erathia's heyday, they set up a fort on the largest island, that grew into a settlement and later, a full-fledged colony.

This place's climate allows for growing tobacco, coffee, sugar cane, and a wealth of exotic fruit and vegetables. The acquisition of this colony was a great success for the Erathians, since previously, they had to import all that from Tatalia. After the demise of King Gryphonheart, however, the ties with the homeland were all but severed, and for a while, the local viceroy felt like the rightful ruler of the archipelago... until the local pirates challenged him, and a war broke out. 

Matters not. The really important part is that these isles are awfully far away from the mainland! And I have not a single clue where Bidley is and where to set sail.
map.h3horn:0.event.5.description:
Back when we were little laddies, mommy used to tell us a tale about the Lodestar. Funnily enough, I've since heard the same tale, word for word, over and over from pirates and devil knows who else. 

"Jeremy-kan?" A voice rang behind me.

"What?" I turned to see Timur. He became a sort of a guide for us, as son as he realized that I was the one in charge.

"I didn’t want to ask. But why did you come here? You fight like a true son of the steppe. You are a warrior."

"Sure, a wa-a-arrior..." I bleated. "I came here to get away from things. But now, I don't know where to go. To find that out, I'd need a Lodestar." 

"Oh, I'd like to sail away too," smiled Timur. "Light the star and sail wherever the heart desires!"

"Ugh. Don't make my life even more miserable." I ruffled up and turned back to the sea.

"But Jeremy-kan! I do know how to light it!"
map.h3horn:0.event.6.description:
I was enjoying the local sour mash while searching my soul. The mash was made from sugarcane. I wouldn't say it was amazing, or even good, but it had to do. At length, Timur entered my cabin, followed by... A thing. Something. If this pile of garbage knows how to get us out of here, I'm all ears. Otherwise, I'd shoot it on sight, just in case.



Upon closer inspection, it was a man clad in some ridiculous robes adorned with feathers, and a hat like a bird's head. A patch of dark skin, a large nose, and a duet of round, expressionless eyes could be seen below the hat.

"This is Crang-Crang," Timur introduced the stranger. "Crang-Crang," echoed the odd fellow for no reason. "Gotcha." I replied angrily. "Better than Abrrgh. So how do you plan to get us to see the Lodestar?"

"Grail," announced the shaman.

"Grail?" I clarified.

"Grail. Bring Crang-Crang Grail. Light Star! Shine!" 



I grabbed Timur by the shoulder and pulled him to the side.

"What in the hell is this? This is the first time I've seen a rat nest talk.

“Jeremy-kan, he is the priest of the local people. A very wise gentleman! Not the best at speaking, though, yes." 
"Shiver me timbers! Is he serious about the Grail?" I sighed.

"I reckon so. You can probably find it if you look at the obelisks. My people have legends... The obelisks depict a map that shows where the Grail is buried," the nomad replied.

"Fine. Go see your buddy out. I don't feel like savoring his tremendous odor much longer. I'll think about what to do."
map.h3horn:0.event.7.description:
Honestly, I only have a most vague idea of what the Grail is. I don't much like to contemplate odd and irrelevant things. It's much nicer to think about gold, rum, and women. The fate commands otherwise, however!



Anyway, about the Grail. I heard that those things once fell from Heavens. Nobody really knows what those are, and how many of them exist. And still, everyone wants one. Well, if Timur is right and the obelisks truly reveal some kind of a map, then why not try and search for this Grail? I'd gladly give up my remaining boot to get out of here and find Bidley. Mommy would never forgive me if I neglected my dear brother.
map.h3horn:0.event.8.description: I began to remember the stories Patris told me... Curses! He was from here, wasn't he? He escaped when their guerrilla squad was captured and his family taken hostage. Such a pity Patris is not with me anymore. He would probably have some errands to attend to here.
map.h3horn:0.event.9.description:
Looks like the local pirates and viceroy are aware of our presence. They clearly dislike the fact that Jeremy Albatross is nosing around. Good! I love making an impression. Our little fortress is attracting more and more people who desire to set scores with pirates or colonists. 



The only thing that truly scares me is that our enemies may find Grail before us.
map.h3horn:0.guards.14.36.0.message: Doesn't look like a free passage. You seem to remember people saying you can only exit here. The key to the entrance is probably somewhere underground.
map.h3horn:0.guards.19.59.0.message: I spotted a boat, turned around, and declared solemnly: "I bestow the name of Black Unicorn upon this ship!"
map.h3horn:0.guards.30.55.0.message: I could never figure out what these obelisks were for. They would reveal some gibberish on touch.
map.h3horn:0.guards.31.29.0.message: You can see the nearby island looming to the west. It's actually not that far away, but no ford in sight.
map.h3horn:0.guards.41.14.0.message: You hear deep, repulsive gurgling, and right away a serpent's ugly head arises above the waves. Taken by surprise, a crewman falls over the poop deck railing. While the serpent is enjoying an unexpected snack, you manage to collect yourself and order the gunners to open fire.
map.h3horn:0.guards.6.69.0.message: You see a company of particularly unfriendly characters emerge from behind a nearby dune. The one in possession of the least appealing mug rises something shiny above his head and starts spouting some balderdash. After he seems to have finished, he proceeds to draw steel, and so do his companions.
map.h3horn:0.guards.71.56.0.message:
Your ship made its way calmly. Suddenly, a huge wave rose straight ahead and fell crashing on the deck. “It's not the sea!” 
You shouted, pulling out your old pistol. 
“It's an ambush!”
map.h3horn:0.guards.8.71.0.message: An item sticking out of sand caught my attention. I leaned in to examine it... Looks like footwear of some sort! Perplexed, my boys watched me furiously digging the thing out. A few minutes later, the sand produced a pair of posh bright-green boots. Exqusitely made, if a bit dirty. Couldn't tell if they were designed for a man or a woman. A fancy thing more suited for balls rather than casual roaming... However, I'd grown way too tired of walking half-barefoot. After brushing off the sand, I put one on. The size was a fine match, as if custom-made to my order! "Nice boots, Cap'n!" heehawed one of the crewmen, with the rest joining his jolly gag. I chortled in response. What the heck. Then I shrugged and moved onward. Lady Luck has smiled upon me today.
map.h3horn:0.header.description: To find his brother, Jeremy must find the Grail and build the Lodestar. If Jeremy is defeated in battle, the scenario will be lost. Leveling is capped at 16. Jeremy will proceed to the next scenario after victory.
map.h3horn:0.header.name: Frontier
map.h3horn:0.monster.20.58.0.message: The hell are you? Begone, this is our boat!
map.h3horn:0.monster.71.2.0.message: Steed for dinner, pirate for supper!
map.h3horn:0.quest.11.59.0.completed: I want you to fetch this thing to an acquaintance of mine. His place is eastward from here. Will you?
map.h3horn:0.quest.11.59.0.firstVisit: You are a stranger here, right? Too convenient! There's a personal matter that I want no one familiar to be aware of. Will you take me up on my offer?
map.h3horn:0.quest.11.59.0.nextVisit: You aren't flying the teal flag. Go away!
map.h3horn:0.quest.42.24.0.completed: Fascinating! This cloverleaf will perfectly fit my plans! By the way, would you care for a little fetch mission? This thingy here is cursed. There's a geezer living to the northeast from here; he might know the way to lift the curse.
map.h3horn:0.quest.42.24.0.firstVisit: I'm expecting a messenger with a package from my friend; it's meant to be some living plant.
map.h3horn:0.quest.66.1.0.completed: My doll! At last! I can cast curses once again! Oh, grand old times are coming back! And to think I had to resort to snake infestations to meddle with my neighbors! That isn't nearly as much fun, and the snakes are growing too big and hard to deal with lately. Will you take them off my hands?
map.h3horn:0.quest.66.1.0.firstVisit: A long time ago I lost a very precious thing. It may not look like much, but it bears some dear memories. Were you to find and bring it back to me, I'd be very grateful.
map.h3horn:0.quest.67.59.0.completed: A demon shoe! Exactly what I was looking for. I'm so very grateful you brought it to me. Now, can you pass this thing on to my colleague? His hut is in the middle of the archipelago. He might want you to do something for him as well.
map.h3horn:0.quest.67.59.0.firstVisit: My friend was going to send me a certain artefact, should he meet someone reliable to pass it along with. Would it, by chance, be you? The thing in question is a big, rusty horseshoe.
map.h3horn:0.quest.71.18.0.firstVisit: A serpent devoured my keychain and scurried away westward. Chase him down and bring back the thing. I will repay the favor.
map.h3horn:0.sign.46.30.0.message: These isles were discovered by the brave seafarer Siagum and her first mate Tsilataf.
map.h3horn:0.sign.64.66.0.message: Serene is imprisoned here. She is guilty of entering the dungeon unauthorized.
map.h3horn:0.town.17.55.0.name: Sharkania
map.h3horn:0.town.32.8.0.name: New Steadwick
map.h3horn:0.town.5.14.0.name: Barkling Bay
map.h3horn:0.town.68.7.0.name: Evergreen
map.h3horn:1.event.0.description:
Bidley had no idea where he found himself. Was he dead? The last thing he remembered was getting sucked into some kind of a swirl. Now, he was in this odd place with the rest of his crew. 



It felt as if he was standing on the seabed. High above his head, he could see fish and huge turtles. Were they swimming… or flying? The only thing he knew for sure was that whatever surrounded him, it wasn't water. Otherwise, he wouldn't be able to breathe or move as freelyas he did. It almost felt as if the air had gotten thick and humid, like some liquid, but runny enough for him to breathe it. 



There was a faded portal behind him. Somewhere on the other side of this portal, there were Jeremy, Tark and that shady Casmetra with the Horn. The realization hit Bidley hard: all of this was set up by the witch so she could get a hold of the artifact! While held in captivity by Dargem, Bidley overheard the renegade mage's rambling. He found out that Casmetra had hired the spellweaver to find the Horn, but when he failed, she got him trapped in a cavern. For that reason, he wanted to avenge himself and take the ancient relic. Bidley wished he'd given it all thought much earlier.
map.h3horn:1.event.1.description:
An odd-looking creature was approaching Bidley's troops... He'd seen others like that before–it was a sprite. Still, he was amazed to see her fly through this “air”. 



 “Wow!” said the sprite in a ringing voice, “these must be primes!"

“Where... where are we?” inquired the confused pirate.

“In the Plane of Water!” replied she, giggling. “Isn’t it lovely here?”

“It is,” Bidley nodded glumly, “but what I'd love even more is to find out how to get out of here.”

“Well, it won't be easy. You'll need to ask Marinus.”

“Where can I find him?”

“There is a town near here–Saltwater. But primes are not welcome there.” 

“Then I'll welcome myself there,” said Bidley, grabbing the hilt of his cutlass.

“Oooh, aren't you one menacing prime!” the sprite giggled again. “Good luck, then. Saltwater is to the east from here.”
map.h3horn:1.event.2.description: Bidley felt sick. He brought his brother into this crazy scheme, and now he lost him. Is Jeremy even alive? Somehow, though, the pirate was sure he would get out of this odd, alien world and find his kinsman.
map.h3horn:1.event.3.description:
Bidley entered a beautiful building of unfamiliar architecture. It must have been a sort of a library. Illuminating the chamber were neither torches nor candles, but odd-looking orbs shimmering with bright whitish-blue light. There were also walls of bookshelves heavy with tomes, and ladders reaching the upper levels. So, a typical library otherwise. 



“And who might you be?” boomed a voice from darkness. 

“I’m captain Bidley,” answered the pirate and turned to whence the voice came, “and I’m looking for Marinus.”

A weird  creature appeared from darkness; it looked somewhat like a human, but with no hair and covered in scales. 

“What do you want from Marinus, prime?” inquired the creature.

“A sprite told me that he knows how to get out of the Plane of Water.”

“Well, she did not lie,” conceded the being. “I am Marinus, the keeper of the library of Saltwater.” 

“Why do you call us 'primes'?” asked Bidley.

“'Primes' is the term we call all who live in your world and others like it. And do not stare at me with such awe. I am a triton. Our race is not very numerous, but some kin of mine dwell in your world too. 



A few minutes later, Bidley dismissed his men; Marinus and he sat down in armchairs.

“Ill timing for your arrival,” sighed the triton. “At present, the Elemental Lords are tied up in a war with Kreegans in your world and fear vengeance from their side. That is why it is hard to get into any Plane, and no easier to get out. You can wait till the fighting subsides.”

“I haven't the time to wait,” the pirate sighed. “My brother may be in trouble. I’ve been betrayed, and I want my revenge.” 
“Then you do not have much of a choice,” Marinus exhaled. “The shortest path to your world lies through the portal in Coralgate. However, the Lord of Water has placed mighty guards there to prevent a Kreegan invasion. They will not let anyone in or out. 

“If I have to fight, I will!” said Bidley with ardor. 
“Not only will you have to fight,” said the keeper, shaking his head, “the Water Lord has also made preparations for the event of the guards falling, however improbable. That is why the exit from Coralgate is locked with the Water Key, Mist Key and Ice Key. And so is the entrance there...
map.h3horn:1.event.4.description: The triton said that the Ice Key can be found in the south-west; it is guarded by powerful icy dragons. To make things worse, Bidley's resources are very limited: he must resort to enlisting creatures from the Plane of Water. It might be a good idea to look for the Mist and Water Keys first; they are guarded by the forces of the Lord of Water. Upon defeating them, more creatures might become available for hire.
map.h3horn:1.event.5.description: Bidley remembered his old dream of floating in the water and being able to see through it as clearly as if it was air. Could it have been a prophetic dream that predicted his journey into the Plane of Water? The thought gave him shivers. “Nonsense! It’s just a coincidence,” Bidley repeated in a bid to comfort himself. Deep inside, however, he knew things were more complicated.
map.h3horn:1.guards.5.40.0.message:
Your crewmen got sight of a wreck, bodies floating by. 
"Some of them poor buggers might have survived, Cap'n… We could use extra hands", uttered a young sailor. 
"Right, matey", you agreed. "Set course to the wreck!" 
On closer inspection, however, all the bodies were already ripe, festering under the sun. You commanded to depart immediately, but apparently the dead were up to shenanigans.
map.h3horn:1.guards.51.107.0.message:
Watching the water surface, you noticed a bottle floating nearby. You ordered the men to catch it, hoping for a lack of evil spirits inside. Soon, a mate ran up to you: 
“Well, I'll be! Maybe it is a message from someone who got trapped here like us?” 
You snatched the bottle from his hands. It contained a piece of paper. Upon reading the message, you realized it being horribly outdated. 
“Author of this letter was Barsolar, cousin of the Immortal King and one of the greatest planeswalkers. He died a few decades ago in Enroth… But if he once managed to get out of here, so can we!”
map.h3horn:1.guards.52.8.0.message:
The General appointed by the Lord of Water to guard Coralgate addressed Bidley from the wall.
“You foolish prime! Do you know what are you doing? You are weakening our forces, and by doing that, you are helping the Kreegans. They are enemies to us as as much as they are to you. So what are you going to do now? Try and assault this impregnable fortress? You are about to perish because of your folly!”
“I will take my chances, if kicking you out of there means getting home!” Bidley's reply was.
map.h3horn:1.header.description: Bidley must capture the town of Coralgate and escape the Plane of Water. If Bidley is defeated in battle, the scenario will be lost. The hero level cap is 18. After victory, Bidley will proceed to the next scenario.
map.h3horn:1.header.name: Heart of Water
map.h3horn:1.town.54.7.0.name: Coralgate
map.h3horn:1.town.86.98.0.name: Saltwater
map.h3horn:2.event.0.description:
Jeremy entered the Black Mark, quickly glanced around, sprawled his hands and let out a jolly wail, “Brother!”

Before he could do anything, Bidley found himself on the receiving end of a bear-like hug. 
“Jeremy! Thunderation! Where have you been? I was just about to go searching for you.
“The Lodestar showed me the way”, answered Jeremy blissfully, letting his brother go. 
“What star?”, frowned Bidley.
“Never you mind. It’s already faded. The places I’ve been to! Cannibal tribes, slave merchants, and all that corn..."
"Lucky you! And I’ve made a trip to the Plane of Water.” 
“What were you up to there?” Jeremy asked suspiciously. “Mostly swimming,” Bidley answered coolly. 

The pirates sat down at the table and traded tales of their adventures for a while, before arriving at the topic of getting coerced into this entire debacle.
“Casmetra”, sighed Bidley, “the witch. She deceived us. She even betrayed her mercenary. Was it… Dargen?” 
“Or Dagrem,” his brother shrugged, “whatever. Jeremy Albatross never forgets a slight! Casmetra will pay for her doings.” 
“Oh really!”, smiled Bidley and sipped some wine, “I thought you were so cute together.” 
“Yes... but what could I do?!” Jeremy made a helpless gesture. “I’ve always been susceptible to beauty and feminine charm! I’m not as square as my brother who is neither interested in women, nor in men nor in mermaids. Ever thought about a career in the Temple of Sun?” “I will surely consider it... once I've strangled Casmetra with my own hands,” Bidley replied coolly. 
“You know what’s the most curious thing about this situation?” Jeremy suddenly inquired in a serious tone, shrugging off the mockery. “She is not even hiding. This witch announced to all of Regna that she now has the Horn of the Abyss. I think Dread Pirate Stanley himself is hiding in his mansion pretending nothing special happened. I managed to collect some information...” 
“They are afraid of her,” Bidley nodded. “The whole goddamned Empire of the Endless Ocean lays low as a bunch of bilge rats, waiting for what comes next. I don’t know why she wanted the Horn so bad, but now we must take it from her. Not only because it’s min… ours, but also because I don’t like what’s going on!"
map.h3horn:2.event.1.description:
Indeed, Casmetra was not ever trying to hide; every drunken sailor in Regna knew she stayed at her residence with the Horn of the Abyss. Tark, an old friend of Bidley and Jeremy’s, was already spying on her. From the very moment Dagrem’s castle cracked open, the nix believed that the pirates would come back some day for revenge. And he was right about it. 

The problem? Casmetra’s island was guarded by hordes of thugs in her service. There were at least four castles; but the witch's exact location was unknown. Bidley, Jeremy and Tark disembarked in different parts of the isle, set up camps and were preparing to assault the lands of the mighty sorceress.
map.h3horn:2.event.2.description: One of Tark’s scouts came back with some information. There is a rumour that Casmetra not only possesses the Horn of the Abyss but also is trying to do something with it, reportedly some manner of a ritual. If that much is true, you must stop her before she succeeds; nobody knows what she is doing, for what reason, and to what possible effect.
map.h3horn:2.event.3.description:
“Yo, brother, chin up! Soon enough, we’ll get a hold of the witch, and she’ll pay for everything!” Jeremy said cheerfully.
“Only if we get to her before it's too late,” Bidley frowned. “I have a bad feeling about her. She knows something about the Horn that we don’t.”
“We’ll hire a necromancer to interrogate her corpse!” the younger pirate roared with laughter and fired his pistol in the air, just to channel some of his youthful energy away.
map.h3horn:2.event.4.description: Another scout came back. He found out about a secret cavern beneath the isle. You should probably look for Casmetra there; just need to find a way to get in there.
map.h3horn:2.event.5.description: It has been a strange day. The sea got very choppy, before suddenly going all calm. It might have been a purely natural phenomenon; still, most of the men under Bidley and Jeremy's command believe the witch and her magicks are to blame.
map.h3horn:2.event.6.description:
It seems that the bad feelings were justified! Hundreds watched the sea tremble and heard it groan, as if it'd decided to jump off its bed before changing its mind.
“Curses!” swore Bidley, “we’d better hurry. I have no idea what Casmetra is up to. Maybe she wants to destroy the Horn, or save the world, or make herself a new broom to ride… but the Horn must be taken off her hands as soon as possible! I don’t like these developments at all.”
“Me neither,” nodded a pallid Jeremy. “What if she wants to awake the Sleeper?” “Who?” the older pirate asked in surprise.
“It all makes sense! To awake Him, you've got to blow the Horn”, Jeremy whispered to himself. Then he looked at his brother and continued, “There’s a legend about an ancient god who slumbers on the seabed...” “Oh, as if things weren't enough of a mess without an old sailor’s scary story on the side,” Bidley brushed him off and went to tend to his affairs.
map.h3horn:2.event.7.description: Today, something odd happened again. Everybody heard a noise coming from the depths of the ocean; it resembled a moan. Time is running out.
map.h3horn:2.event.8.description: Jeremy seems to have goten lost in his theory of a god sleeping on the seabed. He dug up tractates by the ancient mage Joycraft, studied them and arrived at a conclusion that Casmetra is a member of an ominous cult that serves the Sleeper.
map.h3horn:2.event.9.description: It's been overcast and raining hard for two days. There a storm on the sea; it isn't too devastating, but it doesn't look like it's going to subside anytime soon. No doubt it is the doing of Casmetra: as the days grow longer, the storms get stronger.
map.h3horn:2.guards.38.13.0.message:
After the battle, the pirate army took a short breather. Jeremy grabbed a small bag in case there was something of value to loot off the fallen. A bottle of Tobersk brandy from Dagger Wound Islands, too, in order to make the dragging affair less dragging. 
Roaming from corpse to corpse, he spotted Tark nearby. The warrior leaned over each fallen Nix, putting his hand to their chests and saying something barely audible. 
“What are you doing, Tark?” Jeremy chuckled, coming closer. 
“I send them off to their last journey, by our old custom. So did our ancestors, back in the days when the Nixaar Empire was still around.” 
“Nixaar? Never heard of that.” 
“When the world was engulfed in the chaos of the Silence, we dove into the Endless Ocean, and there we built our Empire. We were prospering, until Tritons from the Plane of Water came to attack. The nation was divided. Some died, some fought. And those who survived became slaves to the Overlords. Who was once a slave never forgets what it is like… I fought for the freedom of my people, for them to come back to life and prosperity. And now I'm burying them, killed in a new war.” 
“We are all going to die someday. But nothing goes without a trace, I believe. Our deeds will live on forever!" Jeremy said, smiling. 
“Your brother, Bidley, craves power more than anything else. And what do you wish for, Jeremy Albatross?” Tark asked suddenly. 
Failing to offer an answer, Jeremy took a gulp of brandy and went on, but he left the bag behind.
map.h3horn:2.guards.38.15.0.message:
Among other troops, a group of Nix manned the garrisson walls. Everybody knew by now that they'd become mercenaries, ending up in the service of various Regnan captains upon their liberation from Nighon. And now they were about to fight their own kin. 
Tark, the liberator and ruler of Nix, wanted to bring everybody to reason and urged his kinsmen to join his cause. 
“Brothers, stand by me, like in the olden days! Trouble will befall one who rises against his blood. I don’t want that.” 
One of the Nix in the garrison, apparently their leader, replied: 
“How is the captain whose boot you are licking today better than any other? You betrayed your people, Tark! You deprived us of unity, forcing to join the pirates. I'm not going to kill you for gold. I'll do it because you're a foe! 
These turned out to be the last words of this Nix. Presently, a cannonball swept him from the wall.
map.h3horn:2.guards.59.10.1.message: You seem to be heading the right way. Casmetra is hiding just about here.
map.h3horn:2.guards.74.13.0.message: "Again we become kinslayers", sighed Tark at the sight of the fallen. He grabbed a spade and started digging a grave. Other Nix followed suit.
map.h3horn:2.guards.74.15.0.message: Seeing Tark's troops approach, the enemy Nix got up hissing and shouting "No mercy!". All the garrisoned guard were set to launch an attack.
map.h3horn:2.guards.8.19.0.message: The air in this place is very dusty and dry. It is hard to breathe. Your soldiers cover their faces with scarves.
map.h3horn:2.header.description: Bidley, Jeremy and Tark must defeat Casmetra before she activates the Horn of the Abyss. If Jeremy, Bidley or Tark are defeated in battle, the scenario will be lost. The hero level cap is 24. Bidley, Jeremy and Tark will proceed to the last scenario.
map.h3horn:2.header.name: Horn of the Abyss
map.h3horn:2.sign.40.69.0.message: You are entering the lands of Casmetra

map.h3horn:3.event.0.description:
Bidley and Jeremy were denied their revenge. A defeated Casmetra left everything behind and leapt into a portal; it collapsed right away. The witch was never to be seen in Regna again. Bidley took the Horn, yet he never found out what exactly Casmetra was trying to accomplish with it. 

After a week of fruitless search for the witch, they abandoned their attempts; for all intents and purposes, Bidley was the Pirate King now. 

At that point, Regna was not a recognized state anymore, although it was still occasionally spoken of as “Empire of the Endless Ocean”. Thing is, after the pasing of old Hareck IX, his heir failed to step forward. A power struggle commenced among pirates. In the ensuing turmoil, several captains had proved to be strong enough to seize control over vast territories, but once they perished or lost their edge, chaos resumed. 

Here and now, Bidley was the King, and this word meant not only terror and reverence, but also lots of hatred. Owning a powerful ancient artifact, he could afford to disregard his former peers, the mere seafarers; for fear of the unknown was all he felt. 

The real danger looming was beyond the seas.
map.h3horn:3.event.1.description:
It was a clear day; Bidley and his crew were in a coastal fortress. The Horn of the Abyss was habitually hanging from the Pirate King's belt; he never parted with it. Suddenly, a sailor came running. Visibly scared, he had a scroll in his hands.
“Cap’n, cap’n! I swear by all the sea devils! It was a genie! A genie appeared and told me to deliver this to you!” Dazed, Bidley took the scroll and unraveled it. 
The message read: “I salute you, Bidley Roberts, the new Pirate King! 

I am Solmyr, a modest servant of Gavin Magnus, the Immortal King of Bracada. My lord is disquieted by the news that you are now in the possession of the legendary artifact, the Horn of the Abyss. We reckon that this item must be kept here, in Bracada, under a close watch of the most powerful archmages. You are not a man of science; rather, a bandit and a thief. No doubt your use of the artifact will be ill-purpose: to obtain power and riches, that is. We, the mages of Bracada, cannot stay aside and watch the Horn of the Abyss fall in the hands of a reprobate like you.

Thuswise, I inform you that we are about to send an armed expedition force, with myself personally heading it. I shall not ask you to yield the artefact willingly, knowing that you will refuse in any case. I also bring it to your notice that Elemental Lords are willing to support my lord. They are equally alarmed by the situation, and the Lord of Water is enraged by your razing of the Coralgate fortress.     

To the Pirate King from Solmyr, genie of Bracada.” 

“Check out the big brain on the genie,” Bidley nodded. “Of course I won’t give up the Horn. He can come and take it.”
map.h3horn:3.event.2.description:
Once it became clear that the mages were getting ready to strike, Bidley gathered his men, along with Jeremy and Tark. “That damn Xanthor!” sweared the Pirate King, scanning the horizon through his spyglass.
“Xanthor?” asked Tark in surprise. “The wizard whom I broke out of the barbarian slammer. It was he who told me about the Horn of the Abyss, in 'gratitude' for his freedom.” “And now other wizards want to pop out heads off for the same Horn,” grinned Jeremy. “Indeed, destiny can be as good at humor as I am.” 

“And these Elemental Lords keep getting in the way,” Bidley added, pulling the spyglass away from his eye. 
“At least the Erathians are busy with the Kreegans and aren’t coming to join the fun,” Jeremy concluded. 

“Alright, lads,” the Pirate King turned to his friends. “Time to get ready for a big war. It seems as though Bracada's decided to throw everything they have at us. We haven’t yet fought a foe this strong; but the reinforcements from Regna should arrive soon enough."
map.h3horn:3.event.3.description:
Some unsettling news arrived. 
“Dear brother, you surely remember Dargem,” Jeremy said. 
“That loser who took me prisoner? He lives?”
“He does. It seems as though he's thrown together an army of mercenaries and captains who hate your guts. Long story short, the reinforcements we expected to come from Regna are now with him.” 
“What a turn of events,” Bidley said coldly. “But there's more, right?”
“Yes,” Jeremy shook his head. “Just to round things out, Dargem also brought other guys who like rare artifacts–warlocks of Nighon, that is. It seems he promised them the Horn, while he himself only seeks revenge. Although... no one knows what the hell he really wants.” 
“So many people anxious about one Horn!” laughed the Pirate King. “I wonder how they suppose to split it once they deal with me.” 
“I bet they will start killing each other,” the younger brother lifted his hands in dismay. 
“I sure hope they get at it earlier, so that we may sneak up and cut their throats,” Bidley said grimly, brandishing his cutlass.
map.h3horn:3.event.4.description: It looks like the Elemental Lords conjured their fortresses up somewhere in the north. However, the Lord of Earth has had some problems. His army likely appeared under the ground and found itself in the clutches of Nighon warlocks, who did not expect this encounter at all.
map.h3horn:3.event.5.description: The enemy army grows stronger by the day. Tark thinks it would be a good tactical decision to pit the enemy groups against each other and make use of their weakening. Jeremy reckons that a better option would be to make a sudden strike at the positions held by renegades and mercenaries to capture their weapons and resources.
map.h3horn:3.event.7.description: There are still some people in Regna who resisted Dargem's offers and can be trusted. Loyal captains have promised to send you a ship with supplies.
map.h3horn:3.event.8.description: The ship with supplies has arrived. The next shipment is expected in a month.
map.h3horn:3.guards.128.54.1.message: People of Nighon seem to keep unlucky enemy generals here.
map.h3horn:3.guards.130.53.1.message: “Get out of here, unless you want to join the ones in my cages!”
map.h3horn:3.guards.76.49.0.message: Bidley gave the Horn another rub with a piece of chamois, even though the artifact was spotless. So this is what people coveted so much. Ever since he got to know what the Horn was capable of, his self-confidence was sky high. Still, the thought of fearsome sea spirits obeying his orders made him shiver every now and then.
map.h3horn:3.header.description: Bidley and his friends must defeat all the enemies who vie for the Horn. Bidley must not fall. No hero level cap.
map.h3horn:3.header.name: All hands on board!
