map.h4fact:1.quest.12.48.0.firstVisit: Bring me a capable disciple and I will teach him everything I know.
map.h4fact:1.quest.12.48.0.nextVisit: Unfortunately, I don't feel any knack for magic in you. Perhaps there’s a sorcerer you know?
map.h4fact:1.quest.3.27.0.completed:
The priest takes a long look at each of the artifacts, and finally speaks:
 “You have been of invaluable help to our Temple. I will hand the artifacts over to my brethren immediately. We will make sure that they never harm anyone else. As for the reward... Take this Golden Bow.”
map.h4fact:1.quest.3.27.0.firstVisit:
A robed priest greets you by the hut. He looks you in the eye for a while, and then gestures for you to enter.
“Greetings. I have ventured into these lands on behalf of the High Priest of the Temple of the Sun. Our longtime nemesis, the Necromancer's Guild, is preparing to wage war against us. The Necromancers and their vile creations have been appearing in these wastelands in greater numbers over the recent months. There even are some black knights, or so I’ve heard! We believe that these lands have been home to cursed artifacts since the last century. Their creator was... Bah, that doesn't matter. What does, is that these artifacts must be found and destroyed before they fall into the hands of the Necromancer's Guild. Bring them to us, and I’ll give you something to make it worth your time.”
map.h4fact:1.quest.3.27.0.nextVisit: Haven't found the artifacts yet? Hurry! You may be able to find some of them in old graves and burial grounds, but I suspect some have already fallen into the Guild's hands. You'll have to take them by force.
map.h4fact:1.quest.3.6.0.completed: I had a pair of old enchanted boots lying around somewhere. Oh, yes, here they are! The ogres didn't take them away… they’d never fit over their paws anyway! I have a newer pair, so I don't need them anymore. Do you want them?
map.h4fact:1.quest.3.6.0.firstVisit: You've done so much for me! How else can I thank you..?
map.h4fact:1.quest.3.6.0.nextVisit: Guerhaugh is still around and could return any minute!
map.h4fact:1.quest.30.6.1.completed: Even if there's a clash with Zog himself ahead—Burton has already done everything it can to get me prepared for it. All that's left to figure out is whether I myself am ready.
map.h4fact:1.quest.30.6.1.firstVisit: Today, I had a difficult conversation with Frederick and Sam. I tried my best to make it clear to them: I should be the only one to go to dangerous places. If anything happens to me, Burton and the people who live there can handle it. Just… someone else will take over the scouting. Their loss, however, would be something our town might not survive. “Our town”... Didn’t take long for me to get used to saying that.
map.h4fact:1.quest.30.6.1.nextVisit: This place smells of blood. I can't let my friends take any risks. I'm the one who must proceed here.
map.h4fact:1.quest.31.6.0.completed:
Still fearing a strike of deadly magic from the heavens, you approach the entrance to the cave, but this time with the Orb of Firmament in hand—no lightning bolts this time. 
You will now be able to enter the caves beneath Zog's fortress, but the sphere is best left here at the entrance.
Do you wish to enter the caves now?
map.h4fact:1.quest.31.6.0.firstVisit:
As you start approaching the entrance to the cave, a bolt of lightning strikes the ground right in front of you, out of the clear sky! Then another one, and again, and again... Obviously, it would be deadly to continue on this path.

Without a doubt, these lightning bolts are the work of a powerful ogre sorcerer. The scouts report that Terghez's warriors frequent these caves, and he is rumored to possess a sphere that amplifies air magic. Could it be the solution to your problem?
map.h4fact:1.quest.31.6.0.nextVisit: It is still dangerous to approach the cave.
map.h4fact:1.quest.32.18.0.completed: Seeing gold and gems, pirates are willing to make their ship and themselves available. 20 Crystals, 10 Gems and 4000 Gold will be enough. Do you agree?
map.h4fact:1.quest.32.18.0.firstVisit: Pirates have made camp on this shore. You can hire a ship and a crew here, but only for a hefty fee. Bring 20 Crystals, 10 Gems and 4000 Gold to convince the pirates to join you.
map.h4fact:1.quest.32.18.0.nextVisit: The pirates will not talk to you unless you bring them 20 Crystals, 10 Gems and 4000 Gold.

map.h4fact:1.quest.34.28.0.firstVisit: This road is blocked by a tall palisade with a gate—although it is not clear why; there are no ogre fortresses in this part of the Ravage Roaming.
map.h4fact:1.quest.34.28.0.nextVisit: It seems as though you won't get through here—without the one who locked the gate, it's entirely unclear how to open it. Maybe you should come back here later?
map.h4fact:1.quest.40.6.1.completed: "I see you've got some gems," the minotaur says, shaking his head and just about impaling you with his horn. "Give them over, and you can pass."

A large host of minotaurs clad in dark-armor guards the passageway that leads deeper into the cave.
"Stop right there!” a hulking creature with a blackened horn warns. “This is the training ground for young warriors from Balthazar's Lair. Outsiders aren’t allowed in here. However... for a small fee of 100 gems, we wouldn't mind showing you a few defensive techniques.”
map.h4fact:1.quest.40.6.1.nextVisit: As long as you do not have the agreed amount of gems, Minotaurs are best left undisturbed—they are not to be trifled with.

Do you want to hand over the artifacts and pass?
map.h4fact:1.quest.42.10.0.firstVisit:
There is another ogre garrison here, even better fortified than the previous one. There is no way to storm it. As you are about to turn back, a barbarian calls out to you from the wall.
“Zog keeps everyone in fear, but he hasn't earned any real loyalty. There are some ogres who aren’t willing to kowtow before Zog, but no one dares to stand in his way as long as he has the Iron Fist. Now, if you brought us some very powerful artifacts, such as the Golden Bow, the Angel Feather Arrows, and the Bowstring of the Unicorn’s Mane, Zog would have a hard time duking it out with his rivals. Do this, and we'll let you into his camp, from where you may do as you wish.”
map.h4fact:1.quest.42.10.0.nextVisit: Taking over such a powerful fortification is unthinkable. You can only get through if you bring the artifacts to the barbarians.
map.h4fact:1.quest.42.41.0.completed: “Very well,” says the rogue and reaches for the gems. “Follow me; I'll show you the secret passage. But be careful! The minotaurs aren’t keen on uninvited guests.”

“This is the local minotaurs’ war camp,” he says. “The ogres have tried to barge in a few times, but Balthazar's horned lads know their fortifications.
That said... Get me 15 gems and I'll show you the secret passage into their camp.”
map.h4fact:1.quest.42.41.0.nextVisit: “That's not nearly enough!”, the rogue is outraged. “Got anything else?”

map.h4fact:1.town.15.61.0.event.0.descri: The heroes' success has raised the spirits in Burton: new volunteers can't wait to join the fighters and rid the town of the vile ogres!
map.h4fact:1.town.15.61.0.name: Burton
map.h4fact:2.event.1.description: The scouts brought troubling news. There were several ancient portals in the vicinity of Burton, but everyone considered them long forgotten and their power gone. No one expected them to come back to life anymore, and they were not considered a possible source of threat—but now it seemed as though someone was trying to reactivate them: the air in the portals churned, lights blinking in it...
map.h4fact:2.event.10.description: Today, refugees from faraway Antagarich arrived in Burton. No, not migrants, but refugees! They brought news that made me feel sick and ashamed, as if it were my thoughts that had invited this trouble. Far across the ocean, war had broken out: the Dungeon Overlords of Nighon had joined forces with the demons! It was hard to believe that the celestial guests had found allies so quickly, but facts were facts. Erathia was still reeling from the recent mysterious death of King Gryphonheart, and rumor had it that its capital, Steadwick, had already fallen to the joint forces of devils and overlords.
map.h4fact:2.event.11.description: The pirate spy's loose tongue gave a tip that Dargem's main fortress might be on an island. Indeed it was, but the island was surrounded by impregnable cliffs, and the waves were crashing against them with terrible force. The closest we were able to get for surveillance was at least a mile from the shoreline. If only a way could be found to lure Dargem out of his compound! Could there be any means of communication between the pirate fortresses?
map.h4fact:2.event.12.description: Today we met a merchant captain from Erathia. The war continues, but it seems that there is still hope! Queen Catherine is gathering troops to retake the capital, and she has already chased off several armies of demons and Nighon Overlords! Moreover, according to rumors shared by the same trader, AvLee and Bracada intended to offer assistance to Erathia in its struggle against the demons.
map.h4fact:2.event.13.description:
A merchant from Antagarich brought good news: Steadwick had been liberated! Demons and subterranean creatures are being chased off all over Erathia, and allegedly the land will soon be free of them. 
The trader also shared some bits and pieces of information about the conflict with Tatalia and Krewlod, and the backing that Gavin Magnus's troops had provided to Erathia there, but I wasn't listening anymore...

I no longer thought of the Kreegans as invincible. I still woke up screaming at night when the celestial invaders' ugly countenances sprang up in my dreams, but if humans and elves were able to fight them, maybe we too could get even with them someday. It was, however, neither the time nor the place to think in earnest about it. Burton's needs demanded the full extent of my energy.
map.h4fact:2.event.14.description: According to rumors, Dargem is fortifying his stronghold. If we are unable to defeat the pirate's forces within a month and get to his fortress now, it will be too late.
map.h4fact:2.event.15.description:
Well... the locals who told me that our rule over the local ogres would never last were right.

When we captured Zog's fortress, the high chieftain himself was nowhere to be found. The battle ended when the giant who brandished the Ironfist caught a bomb right between the eyes. We later examined the body—although there was nothing left of his head, the commanders of our allied greenskins were adamant it was not Zog's. Apparently, the Jackal escaped in the last minutes of the battle, leaving one of his henchmen behind to pull the wool over our eyes.

I sincerely thought we had proved our strength and will to the ogres, and that they would accept a non-aggression treaty, if not an outright alliance. I even agreed to yield the Fist to them as a token of our goodwill—I could barely handle that iron abomination anyway. Brum, the ogre who commanded one of our allied forces, and then was elected the new chieftain at a gathering of elders from all local tribes, had promised us peace, but it only lasted a few weeks. Then the news arrived that Brum was no more. On his first trip to gather tribute, the chieftain was ambushed by enemies, and ballista missiles turned him into a pincushion. And the ballistae turned out to be of Burtonese make...

We had Morton in charge of our missile-throwing weaponry; he was an expatriate goblin of a troubled fate and an edgy temper, but a great master of his craft. We summoned him to a council meeting and questioned him whether he knew how those ballistae could have fallen into the possession of our protege's enemies, but he only stared daggers at us, rejecting all accusations. There was no evidence of his guilt in what happened, and we had to back off... but it seemed as though Morton was left deeply offended. 
Just when we were about to send him on a diplomatic mission to establish a semblance of relations with the local goblin tribes. Gods, why is it so hard to govern people?.. and not-quite-people, too!
map.h4fact:2.event.16.description: A sailor who escaped from captivity on Dargem's island said that the pirates there were working frantically to build up their fortress' defences. It looks like we have no more than a month left to take it.
map.h4fact:2.event.17.description: Judging by the news from Burton, the halflings are very alarmed and are summoning everyone who can hold a weapon to join the militia and march against Dargem. We have only two weeks left to capture the pirate's fortress.
map.h4fact:2.event.18.description: The pirates have succeeded in making their fortress impervious. Storming it is no longer possible; even Boyd's power won't help. Our time is up.
map.h4fact:2.event.2.description:
Like many places founded by desperate people willing to do anything in a bid to turn their fortunes around, Burton had its darker moments. One was trade with pirates—not Regnans, but outcasts shunned even by this lawless empire. They eagerly purchased ship's fittings, gun barrels, cannonballs, and other supplies for their unsavory trade. The payment was made in certain rare substances, their origins never inquired about. That lasted but for a short time and only was done out of desperation, but there was no getting away from that piece of history.
As soon as things got better and legal sources for covering provisions and other necessities sprang up, the dealings with pirates came to naught. Chagrin wasn’t nearly strong enough a word to describe the sea rovers’ reaction to this development; they absolutely blew their tops.

“Maybe we're keen on becoming honest traders, too! But nay, cor blimey, turns out our mugs aren’t nice enough for that!” one band’s ringleader, a particularly disagreeable character named Dargem, was seething. “Alrighty, just you wait," he growled. "Time to show these landlubbers that disrespecting business partners carries a price.”

Dargem was as good as his word; several pirate bands conspired to cut off all of Burton's trade routes and began to plunder the supply wagons. The situation was becoming critical.
map.h4fact:2.event.3.description:
An emergency meeting was called to find a way out. There, I heard many stories from the townsfolk about the atrocities committed by Dargem and his cronies. Some were positively chilling, despite the scorching Jadamean sun! 
There was one tale, however, that really piqued my interest; one about a certain Boyd, whom Dargem had allegedly put to an extremely cruel end, even by pirate standards. There were several versions of the story, but they all agreed that a young fellow named Boyd, an adventurer and maverick, had once joined the crew of a brig that flew the Jolly Roger, yearning for new thrills to add to his collection. A natural at telling hilarious stories and singing lewd songs, he quickly became the life and soul of the crew—except the brig's captain, Dargem, didn’t like that very much. 

Himself still quite young for a pirate top dog, he had thus far only mastered one way to keep his crew in line—through fear and threats, that is. He knew air magic, so his threats were not empty; no one wanted to anger him and suddenly die of asphyxiation or, conversely, of ruptured lungs. However, he was also capable of making his ship run faster, using magical whirlwinds to inflate the sails, and of blocking arrows and cannonballs with his air shield. Thanks to that, his men rarely were without rich booty, so there never was a shortage of candidates eager to replenish his crew.

One of them was Boyd, who had so carelessly impinged on the cruel captain’s authority. Was it plain jealousy or something else? Either way, Boyd was doomed. There were many theories as to what had eventually caused the conflict, but an old innkeeper, who had once had the displeasure of having to treat the grim brig’s crew to a feast on the house, overheard a story. According to it, a hapless pirate was made to dance the hempen jig in the blazing sun, but not before making sure the noose would not choke him right away. Guaranteeing that was small challenge for a skilled mage. 

So he hung there, feeding the seagulls, and when the brig called at Jadame's shores, Dargem traded his bones to some grim-looking gangrel for a feather to adorn his tricorn. It is not known what the latter did to them, but since then, rumors have spread of travelers encountering the skeleton of an undead pirate shouting Dargem's name in the night. Some eyewitnesses even added that the skeleton brandished a cutlass, arcane flames burst out of his eyes, and the earth he rode over moaned and swelled. Fear takes molehills for mountains, I thought; but maybe I should try and seek out this undead avenger. As they say, the enemy of my enemy is my... no, not my friend. I'm not keen on being friends with no dead men! Let's say... an ally. Of sorts.
map.h4fact:2.event.4.description:
New times were upon Burton. With the ogre problem solved, along with the issue of securing steady shipments of local products to the market in the port of Orca’s Maw, the prospect of food shortages had receded. The townspeople were now able to make plans for more than just another day's work. Frederick and Sam kept making trips to the port to meet other associates of theirs whom they had persuaded to move to Burton. Some arrived carrying little more than a few books and a toolbox; others brought whole shiploads of alchemical equipment, rare reagents, and instruments. 

A dwarf named Bertram made the biggest noise; rumor had it that the dozens of barrels unloaded from his caravel were brimming with gold. True or not, but soon after his arrival, the town saw a rush of immigrants from all sorts of places, each one getting a job with good pay. New residential neighborhoods sprang up; production was getting transferred from the home forges to the new factory building, its tall vaults supported by steel trusses and beams.
map.h4fact:2.event.5.description:
As immigrants arrived, the first news of the demon invasion's aftermath reached our distant lands. Eeofol has been destroyed. Ravaged. Not one blooming garden left, not one crystal-clear lake. Only endless ridges of new mountains, spewing flames and acrid smoke, hordes of ruthless demons swarming behind it veil. I had seen the possessed Xarfax and the soldiers of his garrison with my own eyes—a horrible and disgusting sight; it seemed, however, that the devils were ultimately unable to subdue many of the other Erathians' minds. Maybe they had learned to protect themselves, or maybe the demons were simply not as powerful as we thought after our first skirmishes with them; whatever the reason, the celestial guests were unable to leap the borders of Eeofol. Even the Fire Coast still remained under Erathia's control, though the awakening volcanoes gave it trouble. 

Talking to those who brought the news, I voiced my rejoicing at the trouble not having claimed thousands of lives in Erathia and AvLee, contrary to our dire predictions born of ignorance—but my heart cried out in pain. It only wondered about one thing: why Eeofol and not Erathia?
map.h4fact:2.event.6.description:
I was no longer helping Frederick in his workshop, as I had my own thing to do now. I didn't even notice how it happened, but at some point everyone began to refer to me as Burton's scoutmaster. Still, I maintained interest in my old friend's progress and knew that he had designed and built an improved steam engine. It was too cumbersome and heavy to be mounted on an airship, but perfect for a factory powerplant; it helped multiply the torque on the metalworking machines’ shafts. Now the factory was building itself: improved machines helped create new structural elements, and the facilities kept growing and expanding.

Frederick was now fully devoted to the energy sector, and had no time to pursue his other old projects. Many of those, however, saw development in the hands of newly-arrived artificers. One, a somewhat odd-looking gray-haired man named Todd, took it upon himself to put automatons into mass production. He spent a good month locked up in a hangar in the company of the prototypes Frederick had brought from Eeofol, a handful of assistants, a variety of tools, and a huge basket of armadillo jerky. When he finally emerged from his voluntary confinement, he looked as if he had never slept a wink in a month—but he was glowing with joy. Beside him, two fully assembled models presented their gleaming, polished sides, and he leaned proudly with his elbow on a stack of blueprints and flow charts. It’s funny to remember how at that moment, my takeaway started and ended with the fact that the pile of papers was noticeably taller than I was—even if I'd stood on my tiptoes.

I had, of course, already seen the automatons preparing our airships, but the other residents of Burton were very impressed when the machines were put on display in the square. Imagine a metal contraption on six mechanical legs, almost the size of a full-grown armadillo, looking like a mix of a crab, a common sight on the shores of the Ravage Roaming, with a carnivorous spider from the Murmurwoods. There was a gurgling sound coming from within the mechanism, and thin jets of vapor escaped from the numerous valves; its steel frame trembled and its joints creaked slightly. The automaton seemed as hot as a water boiler—well, most of it was, in fact, very much a boiler; the powerful grip protruding from a sort of head had a very menacing appearance, and the Burton youths, eager to impress their girls, would time and again run up and stick their hands into the metal spidercrab’s jaws. Little did they know that its superheated steam powerplant in itself could pose much greater danger to others than any kind of jaws or extremities... 

Frederick told me in confidence that Todd hadn’t been able to fully solve its little reliability problem—he only limited the machine’s standard power, but kept the option of switching to the supercritical mode. It was, however, impossible to turn off once engaged. Naturally, the assembly responsible for this feature was taken off the model on display, but I still preferred to keep my distance.
map.h4fact:2.event.7.description:
Burton now smelled of money, and that smell tends to work like a magnet, attracting those who would like to appropriate it, as well as those who are willing, for a fee, to discourage the former. Interestingly enough, the majority of both were of the same pedigree: pirates, that is. Not all of those who used to have dealings with the Burton craftsmen succumbed to Dargem's entreaties to come and take what they needed by force. The more staid ones saw the benefit of going into the rapidly growing town’s service. Furthermore, they were promised the most advanced and powerful weapons crafted in Burton's workshops, and that, of course, was a very good incentive.

The townspeople looked askance at those morose men; the mercenaries, equally effective on land and sea, were mostly employed as bounty hunters. Their arms of choice were arquebuses of enormous caliber and very complicated design. If was easy to see how much care the gunslingers had for the tools of their trade; their brass and steel parts were buffed to a shine and glistened in the sun like jewelry, and hardwood stocks were meticulously polished and varnished. Their cloaks bulged suspiciously at the midriff; hiding underneath were not crude pistols like those used by pirates, but things just as sophisticated and expensive as their arquebuses. Rumor had it that those mysterious weapons had already made countless Dargem's henchmen take dirt naps; a well-trained and disciplined gunslinger always ended up being faster than an ever-drunken pirate and his smooth-bore pocket artillery, however proud a sea dog the latter was.
map.h4fact:2.event.8.description:
An old fisherman came to Burton; he lived on the shore near the little harbor where the pirates used to call at for trade. They’d leave him messages, proposing dates for the next exchanges. He said that he had spied familiar black sails on the horizon several times, more and more often in recent days.

“The blue broad is summoning her gals. And I tell ya, they'll come in force—they all have a husband in every port. Suppose they gather them all, even you’ll be in big trouble, and I'll just get gobbled up, bones an' all. Faces of angels they got, but teeth of sharks…”
map.h4fact:2.event.9.description:
If there is scouting, then there must also be someone to handle the scouts working for the adversary. There was now such a man in Burton, Melchior by name. Sweet-talking and courteous, he could make anyone feel at ease, inducing them to share even what they never realized about themselves. And now he had busted a pirate spy. The interview procedure for those seeking employment as gunslingers, long and confusing for an uninformed onlooker, once again proved to be effective: the candidate broke down over an unexpected question about the best way to spend a large paycheck that came completely against the conversation’s flow. 

At the interrogation, this swaggering, insolent character first laughed and spewed threats, claiming that he feared neither beatings nor death, and that he would certainly be avenged... However, just a minute spent in the company of the automaton that carefully held certain protruding parts of the prisoner's body in its maw was enough; the latter suddenly developed extraordinary eloquence.

Excerpts from the interrogation report:

...lured several enchanters to his side, promising each one a Spellbinder’s Hat...

...fooled the old dolts, of course, but now they seem to have no choice...

...Dargem laughs at your firecrackers and bullets. He's sure he'll squash you like a buncha roaches. What's more, he has several strongholds where his retainers are nested...

...You won't get Dargem. Unless, of course, you can walk on water...
map.h4fact:2.guards.94.15.0.message:
After all the tales I’d heard of the grim dead avenger, I expected just about anything from meeting him, except to run into such a… lively chatter. As I stepped into the hall where Boyd was sitting, he launched into a profanity-laced tirade, something about his endless appreciation for uninvited guests. However, once he got a closer look at me, he erupted with a flurry of compliments, witticisms and jokes just short of ribaldry. Even the light in one of his eye sockets would fade for a moment every now and then, as if he were winking at me.

Before long, though, there was an abrupt transformation about Boyd; it happened the second I first mentioned Dargem. Up until that moment, I could close my eyes and easily imagine talking to a cheerful man brimming with energy and taste for everything around him; yet when Dargem's name was called, Boyd's eye sockets became gloomy hollows, his rich baritone gave way to the whistle of a cold wind mixed with the rattle of bones, and his fingers began scraping at the armrests of his chair with a sickening crunch.

“If you want to bussst that ssstinking bilgerat, I'll do anything to help you. He doesn't know what I've become owing to him; what power I've gained from the emanationsss of torment embedded into my bonesss. But promissse me one thing; once we’ve cornered the wretch, you will let me have him! Much time hasss passed sssince my ssstint on his ship, and he hasss become more than just a go-getting captain—he now hasss his own little realm of brigands he callsss a "principality." He won't ssset a foot out of his castle if he knows we're upon him, but as sssoon as we tread on hisss tail... He'll go chopping and changing. And then we'll make our move.”

For the first time in my life, I felt my feet freezing. Now I knew how those stories of the ghastly dead avenger were born. Indeed: he had only been seen when he was out hunting his murderer, and in that state he was truly awe-inspiring. Of course, no one had ever tried to pay Boyd a visit at his dead manor—and no one knew how tormented that unsettled soul was and how he died all over again whenever forced to remember his last days in that pitiless wretch’s grip.
map.h4fact:2.header.description: You must defeat the pirate Dargem who challenged the people of the wastelands. If Henrietta or Frederick are defeated, the scenario will be lost. Heroes are limited to the level 18. Henrietta and Frederick will bring the components of the Wizard’s Well and the Ring of the Magi to the next scenario.
map.h4fact:2.header.name: Dead or Alive
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.0.text: Dargem hired a whole band of former Regnan sorcerers!
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.1.text: There are some Western Elves among Dargem’s mercenaries. They are said to be excellent marksmen.
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.10.text: A traveler told me that a war on a scale unseen in centuries is raging in Erathia.
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.2.text: Dargem has a sizeable force of shooters.
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.3.text: Pirates have been constantly raiding the lands around Burton in recent weeks. They are even mounting attacks through portals!
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.4.text: Odd creatures resembling giant worms were seen in the eastern mountains.
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.5.text: Smugglers and mercenaries set up camp on the sea coast. I heard they buy artifacts and sell pirate artillery.
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.6.text: Have you heard the story about a pirate captain who lost his memory? They say that many sea dogs now carry pendants to protect themselves.
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.7.text: The Dark Elf Merchant Guild has made its way as far as this remote part of Jadame. They set up a trading post south of Burton.
map.h4fact:2.header.rumor.9.text: They say that the capital of faraway Erathia recently fell, for the first time in recorded history.

map.h4fact:2.heroes.71.biography: All scary stories feature a horseman who had been hanged, stabbed or even beheaded and now rides by night, intending to exact revenge on his killers. Nonsense, a necromancer would say, a dead man risen by himself cannot have memory or will. It may well be so, but then Boyd has scores to settle not only with the traitor who slayed him, but also with the one who denied him rest in peace.
map.h4fact:2.heroes.71.name: Boyd
map.h4fact:2.monster.23.9.0.message: These days, you don't have to wander far to see a honest-to-goodness pirate. Some of them have become so brazen, they come lurking just outside the walls of Burton, catching lead every now and then, sometimes right from the town's towers. This bunch, however, seems new here, just figuring out what to grab and run before a heavy bullet comes their way.
map.h4fact:2.monster.32.12.0.message: These pirates look completely broke and clueless, armed with nothing but crude, short cutlasses. It would seem that Dargem has decided on an endless harassment tactic to wear down Burton's defenders; even if none are killed, the fatigue might come back to haunt them the moment he sends his main forces in to attack.
map.h4fact:2.monster.90.8.0.message: On the road, you meet a limping pedestrian, a pirate by the looks of him, clad in a red camisole, once lavish but now ragged and dirty. It is unclear what he is up to so far from the sea, but he is certainly terrified. You try to talk him up, and at first he is eager to oblige, but as soon as you ask him how he ended up here, he leaps up and lashes out at you. He shouts about having barely escaped from the dead man's dungeon and being loath to let out the secrets he has learned there.
map.h4fact:2.monster.97.7.0.message:
This pirate looks like he's been through the rollers in the crushing room at the processing factory in Burton. He can hardly move his feet, yet he waddles down the road with a look of incredible determination on his blood-strewn face. Upon seeing you, he lets out a shriek:
“He let me go! He said I could walk... give his best to Dargem... I don't care, I'll give it to you... give you a knife in the gut, like he said!”
map.h4fact:2.monster.99.13.0.message: This pirate looks even worse than the first two. He can't so much as speak a word, but it looks as though Boyd has sent him away to carry the same message as the others. He raises his trembling hand with a gun at you. With a sigh, you urge your warriors at him.
map.h4fact:2.quest.104.75.0.completed:
After hearing of the battle with Berhanu's men and your victory over them, the mercenaries agree to let you pass.
Do you want to sail through?
map.h4fact:2.quest.104.75.0.firstVisit:
A small fleet of mercenaries is blocking your path.
One ship’s captain claims that they have come here at the behest of the Merchant Guild to hunt down a notorious thug, a pirate named Berhanu, who has been plundering the Guild’s ships for months. The mercenaries have nothing against you, but they suspect that Berhanu may be using this portal, so they refuse to provide passage to any ships that appear off these shores.
map.h4fact:2.quest.104.75.0.nextVisit: Until Berhanu is captured or killed, the mercenaries have no intention of leaving this bay.
map.h4fact:2.quest.13.18.0.completed: Spend the resources and rebuild the structure?
map.h4fact:2.quest.13.18.0.firstVisit: There is a watchtower here, but Dargem’s pirates laid waste to it during their raids. Rebuilding it would take 50 wood, 20 ore and 12000 gold.
map.h4fact:2.quest.13.18.0.nextVisit: Unfortunately, you don't have sufficient resources to rebuild the watchtower here.
map.h4fact:2.quest.18.5.0.completed: Spend the resources and rebuild the structure?

map.h4fact:2.quest.18.5.0.nextVisit: Unfortunately, you don't have sufficient resources to rebuild the foundry here.
map.h4fact:2.quest.19.32.0.completed: Perfect! This scroll is just what I need! Want to learn the Clone spell?
map.h4fact:2.quest.19.32.0.firstVisit:
Magic scrolls can be very useful, but nothing beats actually knowing a spell. In years past, I instructed magicians in rare spell mastery, and I can help you too. Bring me a scroll with the Clone spell, and I will teach it to you; however, in return I will ask you to give the scroll to me. I know about the pirate raids, so I will not charge you for my services.
Clone spell scrolls are not easy to come by, but I hear one was lost on an island in the bay.
map.h4fact:2.quest.19.32.0.nextVisit: Unfortunately, I can't help you without the right spell scroll.
map.h4fact:2.quest.2.3.0.completed: Aha! That's exactly what I need! Would you like to have the Cape of Velocity?
map.h4fact:2.quest.2.3.0.firstVisit:
Many deal with magical artifacts, but creating them is mostly a lost art these days. I, however, have both knowledge and experience in enchanting items, and I am willing to create a genuine artifact for you.
Bring me 50 mercury, 50 sulfur, 50 crystals and 50 gems, and I will enchant a cape that can increase the speed of your troops in battle.
map.h4fact:2.quest.2.3.0.nextVisit: That's not enough. I need 50 mercury, 50 sulfur, 50 crystals, and 50 gems, no less!
map.h4fact:2.quest.23.52.0.completed:
Hearing of your victorious clash with Yzraal, the smugglers agree to let you pass.
Do you wish to pass?
map.h4fact:2.quest.23.52.0.firstVisit: There's a camp of wererat smugglers up ahead; they won't let you pass while Yzraal, one of Dargem's captains, is nearby. Dargem demands that all profits on smuggling go exclusively to him, and exerts terrible punishment on those who dare to disobey him—Yzraal is here to serve as his eyes and the hand that dispenses his “judgement.”
map.h4fact:2.quest.23.52.0.nextVisit: In the smugglers' den, you could sell some artifacts, buy stolen cannons and even hire mercenaries for various jobs, but the smugglers are terrified of Dargem. As long as Captain Yzraal is around to keep an eye on the den, deals are out of the question.
map.h4fact:2.quest.26.16.0.completed: I see you've found the right men to try out my new weapons. Would you like to reequip them now?
map.h4fact:2.quest.26.16.0.firstVisit: My guns are extremely powerful, but I'm afraid there aren't many in your ranks willing to give them a try. However, I've heard there are some excellent marksmen among the mercenary pirates. Bring a few to me, and I'll be glad to train them in the use of the new weapons.
map.h4fact:2.quest.26.16.0.nextVisit: Still no pirates? I've heard there's a mercenary camp on the coast south of here. The characters there are former pirates who refused to work alongside Dargem. Perhaps they can help you?
map.h4fact:2.quest.28.54.0.completed: Hire 25 pirates for 40 mercury, 40 crystals and 60000 gold?
map.h4fact:2.quest.28.54.0.firstVisit: Mercenaries previously in the service of Dargem stopped at the smugglers' camp on this bay’s shore. The pirates are eager to join your army, if you pay them 40 mercury, 40 crystals and 60000 gold.

map.h4fact:2.quest.34.106.0.firstVisit: These waters are full of pirates, sea monsters and other nasties. Besides, there's always the risk of being hit in the back. Before we go any further, we should capture the pirates' fortress to the east, where Malathi, one of Dargem's captains, has set up shop.
map.h4fact:2.quest.34.106.0.nextVisit: We can't risk sailing further until we resolve the problem with Malathi and her fortress.
map.h4fact:2.quest.4.93.0.completed:
“Bess is done for, ya say? Nice to hear! It's a shame, of course, that we were the ones who tracked her down first, yet she got her comeuppance from you; but what can you do! Well, since we're not going to get the reward now, and opportunities aren’t easy to come by in these parts—mightn’t you have use for some firepower in your army? We could join you.”

Accept the bounty hunters' offer?
map.h4fact:2.quest.4.93.0.firstVisit:
In the hut, you are met by a scowling gunslinger and a handful of his comrades.
"Hunting pirates, huh? So are we. We've been contacted by the Bounty Hunter Guild, all the way from Ravenshore—ever heard of it? A wealthy merchant paid them to find Bess, but they’re failing miserably at the job. The pirate broad has been famously evading capture for a whole year now. Just about everyone was out to get her—trolls, minotaurs, what have you! All for naught. With nothing else left to try, the Guild turned to us. We know for a fact that Bess is out here somewhere, but we haven't been able to pin her down yet, either. You keep your eyes peeled—you might just get lucky, and cross paths with this rapscallion.”
map.h4fact:2.quest.4.93.0.nextVisit: "You say you've never seen this Bess, or even heard of her? Very odd; that gal is hardly the type to keep a low profile. I've heard reports, however, that she'd headed for Burton with her bunch of goons.”
map.h4fact:2.quest.47.90.0.completed: Malathi's band is defeated and her pirate fortress is captured. We can now explore these waters with confidence.

map.h4fact:2.quest.47.90.0.nextVisit: We can't risk sailing further until we resolve the problem with Malathi and her fortress.
map.h4fact:2.quest.48.19.0.completed: Finally! I knew you'd find him! Here, take this magic cloak. I've never worn it. Reckoned my armor would serve me just fine without. Perhaps you could find a use for it?
map.h4fact:2.quest.48.19.0.firstVisit:
In the hut you are met by a sullen-faced dwarf. He grabs his axe, but lowers the weapon after getting a good look at you.

“At last! Thought all I was going to see for the rest of my life were the mugs of those wretched beasts, but lo, a decent face turns up!” the dwarf exclaims. “I beg your pardon. I've seen nothing but ogres and minotaurs these last days. Allow me to share my story. Our ship was sailing from Enroth to Jadame when a sea serpent attacked! Before we figured out what to do, our ship was already going down. By some miracle I managed to make it to shore, and spent the last few weeks wandering the wastelands until I came across this... hut.
 I don't know if any of the ship's crew survived, but my brother was there. I believe he's still alive. Perhaps he managed to get to the other side of strait. If you could find him and bring him here, I would be endlessly grateful.”
map.h4fact:2.quest.48.19.0.nextVisit: Where's my brother? I must see him!
map.h4fact:2.quest.48.27.0.completed: Seeing Tancred, the gunslingers approach you, preparing to declare their conditions.
map.h4fact:2.quest.48.27.0.firstVisit: A group of bounty hunters is taking a breather here. They aren’t opposed to joining your army, but they demand payment, and also stress that they will only talk to their commander, Tancred, who ordered them to stay in this place. One of the gunslingers notes that Tancred was last seen west from here, where he had set up camp.
map.h4fact:2.quest.48.27.0.nextVisit: The bounty hunters will only talk to Tancred!
map.h4fact:2.quest.49.26.0.firstVisit: The Gunslingers and Bounty Hunters are willing to join your army for 20000 gold and 20 gems.
map.h4fact:2.quest.49.26.0.nextVisit: Unfortunately, you don't have the resources needed.
map.h4fact:2.quest.52.36.0.completed: “Wyvern!” The Cyclops squealed with joy. “Brings them here, and Cyclops give worm.”
map.h4fact:2.quest.52.36.0.firstVisit:
The place caught your attention from afar. Surrounded by huge piles of bones, there stood some cages; inside, you could see large sandworms. But it wasn't the worms that caught your eye, it was the two huge Cyclopes standing around a fire that matched their size, slowly rotating a spit with remains of something indescribable roasting on it. 

Jadamean cyclopes are notorious for their immense appetites, and in attempts to sate them, they pounce at humans, ogres, and trolls, and sometimes even dendroids. These Cyclopes, however, did not seem to be intent on attacking you. 

“Some sour mug again,” one of them suddenly rumbled. “Peoples thinks us bad guy! And why? Cyclops not man-eater. Cyclops trapper. We catch rare beastie, and dark elves gives meat for good beastie. Why not trade with us, too? We have worm. Cyclops can give worm.” 
“I'm afraid we have nothing you’d like.”
“You sure? Well, if finds wyvern, brings them. Cyclops trade for worm.”
map.h4fact:2.quest.52.36.0.nextVisit: It seems the Cyclopes are still here, and you have nothing to interest them.

Are you willing to part with the artifact?

map.h4fact:2.quest.56.30.0.nextVisit: The Liches are undeterred. They will not let you pass unless you bring them the Dead Man's Boots.
map.h4fact:2.quest.58.63.0.completed: After positioning the rings in their proper places, you are pleased to see that the chest can now be opened. Inside, you find a magical shield made of dragon scales. Do you wish to take it?
map.h4fact:2.quest.58.63.0.firstVisit:
If it weren't for your guide's hint, you wouldn't have noticed a thing here. Following his advice, you spy a bump, which on closer inspection turns out to be a great chest plastered in mud and grass. After brushing them off, you find ornaments depicting dragons and snakes. Apparently, this chest has been here for a very long time, maybe ages, but no one has managed to open it so far.

Indeed—you cannot find a gap between the lid and the walls, nor a keyhole, but among the ornaments you notice two small holes shaped like dragon eyes... or rings with dragon eyes?
map.h4fact:2.quest.58.63.0.nextVisit: You still can't open the chest. The only thing you can do is look for the keys to it.

“Excellent! Now we can return to Alvar. Oh, yes, the mountains... Follow me; I'll show you the way. And be careful—lots of ghost dragons have been seen around these parts. Must be the work of the exiled necromancers who have settled in these lands.”

Do you want to proceed to the mountains?
map.h4fact:2.quest.64.3.0.firstVisit:
In the mountains, you meet a group of traveling dark elves. They appear to be in search of something.
"I collect rare military decorations," one explains. "It is said that during the Ogre-Goblin war, several valuable specimens were lost in these lands. If you can find me some, my friends and I will help you climb the mountains. Without an experienced guide, you’re going to lose your heads here.”
map.h4fact:2.quest.64.3.0.nextVisit: "I see you haven't found the decorations yet. Well, we'll be around for a while, so you can take your time.”
