map.h4fact:3.quest.36.82.1.firstVisit:
In the far corner of the cave you meet a group of Efreet. Their leader calls out to you: 
“Freedom! We have waited too long for this moment. When the Silence came over our world, we refused to guard this tomb. For that, we were imprisoned in the caves, and Phlegeth stayed behind to guard us. Please, allow us to go with you and finally leave this place!”
map.h4fact:3.quest.38.89.0.completed:
As I suspected, we found some slightly battered plates and levers of shining metal in Gorghe’s treasury. These were the missing parts—it seems the goblins really thought they were gold. Of course they did! Beryllium bronze isn't easy to tell from gold, unless you're an alchemist. There's concern that the goblins may have badly damaged the automatons when they took the parts out, but there's only one way to find out for sure.

Try to activate the automatons?
map.h4fact:3.quest.38.89.0.firstVisit:
While exploring the goblin village, I decided to take a look inside an old, dilapidated pen. Inside, I was surprised to find... automatons! Piled carelessly into a heap, they didn’t appear to be beyond repair, but were obviously malfunctioning. In Volta, the local mechanics told me that a few months ago, before the worms came to the land, one of the local manufactories had been attacked by goblins who trashed the place so badly, it was impossible to tell what they'd stolen and what they'd simply smashed to bits.

Surprisingly, it seems that these mechanisms traveled here on their own, but we can’t activate them right now; some key parts are missing. Maybe the local barbarian chieftess decided she's a great inventor, and we can find some parts in the goblin fortress she resides in?
map.h4fact:3.quest.38.89.0.nextVisit: The goblins and their leader, Gorghe, still control the fortress. The nearest operational manufactory is too far away, so the only way to activate the automatons is to take the missing parts from the barbarians’ clutches.
map.h4fact:3.quest.39.157.0.completed:
When the engineers see Mormolykos’ Cowl, they immediately express their willingness to go with you. They are surprised to learn that the vampire has been found so far away, but they nod understandingly when they hear your story about the old mansion.
Do you want to take the Engineers with you?
map.h4fact:3.quest.39.157.0.firstVisit:
At the foothills of the mountains, you find a small mining camp and a group of armed Engineers. Upon hearing about Henrietta's missing expedition, they express their willingness to go with you, but unfortunately they cannot leave the camp unguarded because the vampire Mormolykos has recently been seen by the village, with several miners falling victim to him.
If you could track the vampire down and destroy him, the engineers would join you on your quest.
map.h4fact:3.quest.39.157.0.nextVisit: Engineers believe the settlement still needs guarding. The vampire could yet return.
map.h4fact:3.quest.4.59.0.firstVisit: The road to Palaemon's fortress is blocked by a wall. As you look closer, you notice a large gate that seems to be sealed with magic. The only way to break the seal is to use the Ring of the Wayfarer.
map.h4fact:3.quest.4.59.0.nextVisit: The wall is indestructible, and you haven’t found the ring yet. Perhaps we should search for it in the tomb east of here.
map.h4fact:3.quest.4.60.0.completed:
In Dryope’s fortress, we found an odd-looking gemstone cut in the shape of a cube. I pointed it in towards the diamond giant and pronounced the golem deactivation spell I remembered by heart from my first year in the Academy. Presently, the giant froze like an ordinary—well, surely not quite ordinary, but still a statue.
"Great stuff," I nodded to Kastore, suggesting we proceed towards Palaemon's fortress.
"We should be careful," Kastore said, raising an eyebrow. "I feel the presence of a very powerful sorcerer. A mind mage.”
map.h4fact:3.quest.4.60.0.firstVisit:
Before me stood an unspeakably large diamond golem. The colossus, hands on his hips, gazed at us silently.
Finally, he spoke.
“Cannot let you through. Dryope ordered no one to be allowed in or out except Dryope and Palaemon. You are not a Dryope or a Palaemon. The order stands.”

"I don't recommend you try fighting this thing,” Kastore said. “Especially without my help, and I would hate to waste my powers while we are still far from our goal. Perhaps we should seek out this Dryope? It is unlikely that she will understand our situation, but perhaps we will find something on her that will be of help.”
map.h4fact:3.quest.4.60.0.nextVisit: The diamond giant silently glares at us. There is nothing to do here—I can only follow Kastore's advice and seek out Dryope.
map.h4fact:3.quest.43.113.0.completed:
I watched the battle from the hill and saw your victory. You humans value gold above all else, but I cannot pay you. You could settle for this herd of armadillos, maybe?

Do you want to accept the reward?
map.h4fact:3.quest.43.113.0.firstVisit:
When you enter the tree hut, you find a troll. His heavy club is lying on the floor, and he doesn't seem to notice you at first. Finally, he turns to you.
“Leave me alone! I'm disgraced. I was known as the strongest warrior of my tribe, but a while ago, returning from a hunt, I found my village burning. I followed the track and found an army of undead with a death knight in command. They are way too strong for me, so I can't avenge my tribesmen... Or maybe you will help me? Our tribe has never been too wealthy, but I may have something to thank you with.”
map.h4fact:3.quest.43.113.0.nextVisit: I know that Thammus the Death Knight still walks the earth. When the mountain collapsed, his army was trapped too. They couldn't have gotten far!

map.h4fact:3.quest.61.3.0.completed:
"The dragons in the Hall of Illusions… gone?” the lich asked, his voice tinged with doubt. “Now then," if a clean-picked skull could grin, you'd swear he did just that, "I have little reason to distrust you. You can go to the portal, and we are taking our leave. There have been no new orders from Trophon, and we do not enjoy being left holding the bag out here.”

Would you like to pass?
map.h4fact:3.quest.61.3.0.firstVisit:
As we turned toward the canyon, we failed to notice the ambush in time. Ahead of us, a large host of vampires stood prepared to fight, and on the cliffs above, liches towered, holding their deadly staffs at the ready. Before long, one of them, dressed in lavish robes, headed in our direction—clearly the leader of the party. He waved his bony hand at the undead threatening our troops, and they retreated.

"We don't care what mages do in these lands," the lich said. "We came here on Trophon's orders, and you do not concern us. I will say one thing: Trophon told us to prevent anyone from approaching the portal until the problem is solved.

"The problem?" Kastore inquired calmly, as if oblivious to the hordes of undead surrounding us.

"The necromancer Meline fled to these lands. She has violated the laws of the Guild and is now conducting unauthorized experiments to create undead dragons.

"That much we already know," Agar grinned, stroking his beard. “Don't waste your time telling.”

“I do so commend your cognizance. What you probably do not know, however, is that some of the dragons are now out of her control. Meline herself is no longer our concern, as Trophon has personally set out to hunt her down; however, we have been tasked with locating and destroying those creatures. They are said to have hidden in the so-called Hall of Illusions, but we have already sent warriors there, and none have returned. That is why we are waiting for reinforcements now. However... we would not mind in the slightest if someone else dealt with them. Maybe we would even let this bold soul through to the portal. They say it leads to another part of the Tomb.”
map.h4fact:3.quest.61.3.0.nextVisit: The undead army is still guarding the portal. Until the dragons in the Hall of Illusions are destroyed, it's best not to risk getting involved with them.
map.h4fact:3.quest.63.22.1.completed:
The treasury was brimming with all sorts of weapons—magic swords, spears, bows and slings. There were even Burton-made guns; no idea what the Necromancer meant to do with them.

Shall we take the weapons and equip our forces with them?
map.h4fact:3.quest.63.22.1.firstVisit:
The Necromancer Meline’s laboratory was a very imposing place. In one corner, I could see enormous flasks filled with bubbling liquids; odd-looking vessels dangled on chains attached to the ceiling; and in front, in a wide cavern, I could see three dragon skeletons chained together.

On one of the tables littered with magical treatises, I noticed the Necromancer's journal.
The last entries were telling enough:

“...February 5. Another experiment has failed. The soul jars were destroyed, and the dragons died for good. Perhaps black dragons are not fit for this purpose. 

February 24. My undead managed to capture three green dragons in the nearby cave. There's no reason to be discouraged—I'm sure I'll succeed this time.

February 25. Another miscalculation, and another failure. I suspect I'll have to send the undead out to find me a new dragon. Besides, one of the ghosts told me old Trophon's nosing around. That's the last thing I need. I can't afford to lose this lab too...”

“What's going on here, anyway?” I said in surprise, closing the journal and looking around.

Agar didn't seem perplexed by the weird laboratory.
“It is plenty clear what’s going on here. Someone was trying to create a lich dragon. Again. The long-established fact that it is completely infeasible doesn't seem to be stopping anyone from trying. You know, the same problem as with certain not-so-sensible artificers and their silly ideas of a perpetual motion machine. Except that their inventions, at worst, just explode, while this thing here can yield some really rotten fruit!”

“Oh, please! Back in Bracada, my colleagues also told me that—”

Remembering something from the past, I almost allowed myself to take offense at the lippy old man; but then Kastore, who’d been silent until that moment, entered the conversation.

“If we had less to worry about right now, I'd tell you something about the perpetuum mobile, my esteemed... scholars. But look here, what is this?” His attention got drawn to a closed door in the lab’s corner.

“I bet it's a treasure room. And sealed with magic, too!” Agar perked up. “Maybe that boorish bone-bag, Trophon, who came here looking for Meline and her lab, took some sort of a barrier-breaking orb, or something, away.”
map.h4fact:3.quest.63.22.1.nextVisit: You can't open the treasury; you must find the orb that can remove the magic barrier.

map.h4fact:3.quest.86.32.1.completed:
Upon swallowing a fabulous amount of valuable resources, the box emits a pleasant ringing; on the luminous plate, which, as Kastore suggests, is called a "screen," an image of an artifact appears, together with the words:

"Required materials deposited
Grant the wish?
To confirm, utter 'Yes'"

Receive the artifact?
map.h4fact:3.quest.86.32.1.firstVisit:
After regaining control of his pets, Agar lost interest in what was happening around, produced something like a conductor's baton out of his satchel and began waving it, loudly humming some odd tune. A huge swarm of worms began synchronously twitching their tails to the beat.

Kastore let out what sounded like a stifled chortle and invited me to enter the rickety hut. Inside, we found a large, dented metal box, demonstrating obvious traces of Olgoi-Khorkhoi teeth. I went up to it and picked at a row of button-like protrusions with my finger. Suddenly, from the depths of the box, an intermittent squeak came, then a screech, and finally, one of its walls opened like a window turned sideways. The lower half looked like a receptacle, and on the top half, something like a magic ball, only flat, lit up. Letters and symbols appeared on it, the language I'd already seen in the halls. I grimaced and muttered "I don't get it"; and then suddenly the unintelligible scribbling gave way to letters of the Erathian alphabet.

"Wish Granter 066085 ready to work
Available granting cycles: 1/71
Scanning your wishes..."

Before I knew it, the magic inscriptions changed. Now they said the following:

Wish defined as desire to possess the missing
Granting challenge: 1/10
Granting cost: 10/10
For granting, place the following in the receiver:
100 units of ore
100 units of wood
100 units of sulfur
100 units of crystals
100 units of mercury
100 units of gems
50,000 units of gold"

While I was trying to figure out what all this meant, Kastore shouldered me away from the box and began poking his fingers at various protrusions and circles that seemed to represent its controls. Each touch was followed by an irritating squeaking sound and a red flash.

"Well. It looks like this machine is either semi-broken or not designed for manual input. However, if the worms were able to get it to grant their wishes of obtaining a sense of beauty... I reckon it will not let you down with yours either, my friend. At least it can read minds for sure. By the way, what is this 'desire to possess the missing' about?"

"I think I know. I figured out at my leisure how to assemble an interesting piece from some of the artifacts that we found, but there is one more item needed to complete the formula. I was just thinking about it when we came here..."

"Damn it, why didn't I get to the machine first?! We are unlikely to be able to recharge it. Oh well. So are you going to get it to grant your wish? We don't have much to invest our riches in now anyway."
map.h4fact:3.quest.86.32.1.nextVisit:

"Insufficient materials for granting
Deposit the specified amount"

At last! We can now head out on our expedition. Per one of the engineers, the airship yard is to the west—the road along the bank of Silver Creek will lead us straight to the moorage. The engineer warned me of a large den of green dragons nearby, but added that these beasts don’t tend to attack for no reason.

Do you wish to pass?
map.h4fact:3.quest.95.176.0.firstVisit: We have a long expedition ahead of us, but we are not yet fully prepared for it. The airship is in excellent condition now, but there might be malfunctions on the way, so we need to make sure we have everything we need to repair it and manufacture the necessary magical devices. 10 mercury, 10 sulfur, 10 crystals and 10 gems would suffice, in my estimation.
map.h4fact:3.quest.95.176.0.nextVisit: These supplies will not be enough. We’ll need 10 mercury, 10 sulfur, 10 crystals, and 10 gems, no less.
map.h4fact:3.quest.95.21.0.completed:
As soon as the statue is in place, a strange rumbling sound is heard. The passage to the depths of the tomb is opened by some unknown force.
 When you look inside, you are surprised to see not the tomb’s walls, but caves that go deep underground. It's hard to say why Henrietta and her expedition headed here—but at any rate, they're definitely somewhere ahead. All that's left is to find them.
Would you like to head into the caves?
map.h4fact:3.quest.95.21.0.firstVisit:
Up ahead, you see a sealed entrance that leads deep underground to the far section of the tomb. You notice the footprints of humans and halflings, not yet covered by sand. No doubt Henrietta's expedition was here not too long ago.
 Attempts to open the entrance have failed. You notice an unusual pedestal, on which a huge statue clearly once stood. Strangely enough, there's no trace of the statue itself anywhere. Perhaps you should go look for it?
map.h4fact:3.quest.95.21.0.nextVisit: The passageway is still sealed, and attempts to get inside have come to nothing.

map.h4fact:4.event.1.description:
It was still dark when wagons appeared outside Bertram's shop. Of course they did! Those were the dark elves, Bertram's "colleagues" in the Merchant Guild. Probably delivering another shipment of rare materials. 

If only things were going as smoothly for me! The first few days of work on the gantry design I'd invented went as well as could be expected. Then, I realized that the intended plan might call for way too much metal. Alas, our smelters are not operating at full capacity, as Burton's mines are almost depleted. Sure, raw materials can always be acquired on the market, but the greedy merchants charge an arm and a leg. Damn elves!

I was walking back to my shop when one of the mechanics called out to me.

“Todd!” he shouted. "We found out something about the minotaurs that attacked the mining camp. They came from the caves nearby. And that’s what’s weird about it... See, Balthazar's minotaurs had left those caves a long time ago—try decades. So I'm guessing the attacks aren't their doing.”

“Maybe it's some bandits or renegades?” I suggested. "Wait… What were you saying about the caves?”

“Those are in fact old mines of the Dark Dwarves, the Minotaurs’ longtime enemies. They are known to have once been very rich in iron ore, rock crystal and other minerals. Half a century ago, the Dark Dwarves kicked the horned ones out of there and have since been sitting on those priceless materials like a dog in a manger.”

I pondered.

“Odd indeed. How did the Minotaurs end up there again, then? It’s worth a thought... Is there much ore left there? Maybe that's where we could get the materials to build the gantry.”

I gave the mechanic a smack on the shoulder and went to my workshop, laid out the drawings on the table and plunged into reflection.
map.h4fact:4.event.10.description:
Things are going from bad to worse. Jangaard’s been watching Todd's shop lately, and he reports that my rival’s first gantry is nearing completion. He is almost ready to begin assembling the first dreadnought.
I have only a few days left. It's time to switch my shops to 24-hour operation and increase overtime pay, or all the great work I’ve done will be for naught.
map.h4fact:4.event.2.description:
Things are going from bad to worse. My sources close to Bertram report that his first gantry is nearing completion and that he is about to begin assembling the first dreadnought.
I have only a few days left. I must put everything I have in me on the line, or it will all be just a big waste.
map.h4fact:4.event.3.description:
I have long gotten my name inked into history. Sure, there was a time back in the day when that dwarf Bertram kept appropriating my inventions and profiting from them, despite having put no effort into them, save for a handful of gold. Much water has passed under the bridge since. Today, you’d scarcely find one in Jadame who hasn't heard of my self-propelled steam engines, the Automatons! Ol’ Redbeard may insinuate all he wants that I merely took apart and put back together what Frederick had done before me... Nonsense, all of it! Granted, I indeed got the prototypes from Frederick, but, for crying out loud, they are based on a theory developed a good two centuries ago by our common ancestor! And what a great, undeservedly forgotten man he was—but he ended up getting blotted out of the Bracadian annals. Only his diary, signed with the enigmatic initials—D.P., and a portrait, which I keep in a special place in my workshop, have survived. Frederick proposed the powerplant solution, but the mechatronics, the strength calculations, the control equipment, the unique hydraulic logic machine—that was all me!

It is now time to prove once and for all to that peddler, and to all of Jadame—no, to the whole world—that talent can't be bought! Either you have it, or your name is Bertram. I've been waiting for this for a long time, too long. Here was my chance to finally get even with that wheeler-dealer for his patronizing tone and vile irony; tread him down and humiliate him so that everyone can see his shame! My invaluable experience as an inventor, my golden hands—and a little elbow grease, but that's up to Sam; I'll admit she's not a bad mechanic.... All we have to do is to perfect what’d been brewing in my head for so many years. Now that’ll be a proper snub on the nose for this so-called "Guild," only good for snatching honest bread out of the hands of humble geniuses. Like myself.
map.h4fact:4.event.4.description:
Lamp oil that burns brighter than any candle—just a cup of it will keep your home lit all night. Rope woven from the finest unicorn hair, with a core of pure spider silk, that can keep a black dragon at bay. Bombs that can tear up rock in your mines or turn hordes of your enemies into so much mush. You want it? It’s all yours, my friend. As are hundreds of other items offered by the Merchant Guild of Alvar! I was already wealthy and successful in business back in Antagarich, but I had not the slightest idea of the possibilities membership in such a powerful company offered. 

Our artificers here wouldn't have been doing half as well if it hadn't been for the Merchant Guild. It was I who reached an agreement with its representatives, and they now cover the supply of rare materials and reagents from all over Jadame. This deal earned me a seat and a vote on the Captain-Director Council.

I've always said it, and I'm ready to reiterate it again: budget planning is key to any inventor's work, and at least half of his success depends on it. Now consider Todd's recent accomplishments: most credit for them should go to those who have taken it upon themselves to handle the boring paperwork, the uninterrupted supply of materials, and the outfitting of his shops. This puerile, careless… moth in a man's body… he flew down to Burton and somehow persuaded his kinsman that he could run a manufactory! 

Had I not long known Frederick myself, and had I not read in his eyes the silent plea to help the old airhead out... Look at him now: he has just barely made something out of himself, and makes it look like he doesn’t need the Guild anymore! Like we’re now irrelevant, only remembered of when he decides to whine some more about the interest rates! Highway robbery, he dares call it! Little does he know that our rate accounts for dozens of criteria and uses formulas several times longer than the most complex thing he had ever been able to conceive of in his entire life! You know what, buddy? That’s it. I've got a waiting room full of guys like you right now. Each one smarter and quicker than the last. Where would you be with your steam-spitting stilt-walkers, hadn't I sneaked three of my best process engineers onto your team? Men I invested ten years of my life into, hammering the understanding of how a real factory works into their heads? You would still be out there, polishing and grinding every rivet and nut, for you were never capable of stopping and soberly assessing the prospects of what you do. 
The artificer is just a cogwheel in the machine, and I can easily find one whose teeth won’t strip. Money is not of concern, for taking an ingrate down a notch is priceless. What can he do without us backing him? Make people laugh as his newest contraption stumbles a few steps, cuts a loud one and falls apart?! Meanwhile, we the Guild can guarantee you: however challenging the order, it will be completed on time and to the highest standard!
map.h4fact:4.event.5.description:
Todd was giving his newest invention a trial. With each new run, the mechanism worked better and better. In his dreams, he was already riding the mechanical beast away, to some place where wooded mountains meet the blue sky. Ah, if only he was ever able to complete a single device in its entirety! Not just another peculiar buzzing motor with legs, but a proper... he had long ago come up with a word for his dream machine: a sentinel, one of his very own design!

As Todd was alone with his thoughts, the workshop’s owner, Bertram, was sitting at a desk in the corner, tallying up the books and jingling coins.
Todd shook off his dreamy attitude and spoke, as if to no one in particular:

“Have you, just once in our life, created anything that you could be truly proud of?”

The dwarf wrinkled his nose and silently went on about his thing.

“No, listen to me, you paper worm; have you ever dreamed of an alloy that makes chisels stronger than granite; of a perfect gear tooth shape that just works, without any backlash or seizure; of a tool whose touch instantly vaporizes the part of a metal workpiece you want gone? Ever begged the tip of a hair-thin drill bit not to snap off when failure would mean a year's work wasted?”

The dwarf grimaced. He was almost done counting the proceeds.

“Hey you old ginger mop, do you know the feeling when the last roughness in your mechanism rubs together, making it sing like a magic cricket from the forests of AvLee? Of welding a solid seam in two passes where no one else would have used less than five!”

The dwarf was done counting the money. Down to the last coin. He locked the pouch in the drawer, looked up and asked:

“Got any idea why no one likes us dwarves?”

Todd replied:
“‘Cause you're fat, boring, earthbound!”

" ...and greedy," Todd added and turned to the window. Something glistened on his cheek.

Bertram stroked a curl of intricate carving with his finger and whistled. The desk made a long, rattling sound and stomped off into the far room, with smoke billowing out of the inkwell. The dwarf pulled his glasses down to the tip of his nose and eyed Todd up. The young inventor sighed heavily and waddled over to the drawing board.
map.h4fact:4.event.6.description:
It had been decades since. Todd no longer worked for Bertram; he had moved back to his homeland of Bracada. He struggled to find any like-minded alchemists there, however, and continued his research alone. He lived a life of modesty, but his wants were meager, and he was able to cover the cost of tools and materials by occasionally selling amusing mechanical toys to the well-to-do and aristocrats. He was ignorant, however, of the fact that the very same dwarf was behind advertising his creations. Bertram no longer had hope for his former protege to ever master the art of handling serious projects, yet still he was loath to let him out of sight—after all, Todd’s head was positively brimming with invaluable insights. 

Besides, somewhere in the back of his mind, he retained a semblance of warm regard for the man who had once come to his workshop as a skinny, doltish teenager. Todd eagerly studied everything the dwarf had to offer before coming to believe that he had left his mentor far behind and that it was time for him to leave this golden cage. Cage or not, it was golden indeed; Bertram didn't pay Todd much in terms of money, but the apprentice never wanted for anything, and not even the smallest request of his was ever refused, provided he could explain how it would benefit the work. Precisely this last point was, however, often the root of the problem: Todd felt the mechanisms like his own gut, but to explain the essence of this or that effect, achieved or supposed? And to do it clearly and consistently? That was beyond him. 
Humans... so hurried, so unreliable, so fickle, and their lifespans so short. Todd was graying already, and his head trembled visibly as he thought, while Bertram was still in the prime of his dwarven years. Still, the time seemed to have only reinforced their desire to prove something to each other.

The former companions had parted ways long ago but eventually ran into each other again—in Burton. One had grown used to thinking that he was capable of anything and that all he needed was to let his thought fly free, so it would return stronger and find material embodiment. The other believed that a solid base was primary; in his opinion, with work well organized from the outset, success would surely follow, however challenging the job. 

Little did they know that there was also a third person in this equation—he, however, chose to remain in the shadows for the time being. He put himself on the other side of the equal sign; the entire sum of efforts by the former two was meant to go to him.
map.h4fact:4.event.7.description:
Burton was once founded near an ore mine, a scarce luxury in the region, but now its reserves are almost depleted. The wastelands are not called the wastelands for nothing: they are poor in resources, and we now must trade for them, paying with our factories’ products. Most of them go to cover internal needs, as development swallows rolled metal, castings and everything else like a bottomless pit, leaving only meager crumbs of the total output to be traded. Of course, customers are willing to pay for them very dearly, but construction on this scale takes a lot of resources. And by that I mean a whole lot.

And then there are the surprise attacks on our supply trains by minotaurs and other rabble. The minotaurs of Jadame had never previously been overtly hostile to their new neighbors; they seemed to be content with keeping to their underground labyrinths, only ever coming to the surface out of some dire need.

Whatever the reason for these depredations, the timing couldn’t have been worse; the competition of the century is at risk!
map.h4fact:4.event.8.description:
Today is a big day. Sure, when deadlines are tight, every hour counts, but this day is truly exceptional, so I had no choice but to halt the work for a bit. We had to get prepared and clean up at least a little bit, so as to avoid making asses out of ourselves with the distinguished guest watching. Frederick arrived at my workshop with his new acquaintance, Kastore, the king of faraway Deyja, for a joint inspection. 

I had always imagined that kings were all about indulging in luxury and slapping their servants around; imagine my surprise when I learned that even before the competition began, Kastore had been personally involved in research into the artifact Henrietta had brought back from the Tomb and developing the beam generator prototype. I have no idea how, but this warlock seems to know way more about technology and process physics than all of us put together!

So it must be true what they say: these sorcerers make a deal with the devil to gain their knowledge. Or the devils... Frederick had shared with me some observations he'd made while examining the odd celestial bodies those uninvited guests had ridden on their way here. Ah, never mind that. Today, the two men looked around my workshop, checked out the blueprints, and entered into an argument. 

Once done with that, they turned their attention to me, and Frederick was the first to speak. He was clearly pleased by the pace at which the construction was progressing; invested as usual, he asked me countless questions about the minutiae and my plans for the future. Kastore, however, was the complete opposite. Nary a muscle moving on his face, he just crossed out a few formulas in the calculations and values on the drawings, filling in others instead. Then, with the same deadpan expression, he inquired whether I needed any new materials or tools, commented that our work processes dearly needed adjusting, and left. By evening, I learned from my trusted connections in Burton that I had passed the inspection, but so did my rival. The entire town’s workflow was to be reorganized, with Kastore leading the project personally.
map.h4fact:4.event.9.description:
I had to get up early, for a caravan setn by the Dark Elves of Ravenshore was arriving in the morning! My colleagues in the Merchant Guild were delighted to treat me to regular supplies of select raw materials for my experiments... for a price, of course.

...I knew something had gone wrong the moment I saw the empty wagons. The caravans were usually accompanied by guards, but this time there were none around. Moreover, the wagons themselves were suspiciously few.

“What happened?”, I finally implored one of the merchants.

“I mean, isn’t it kind of obvious? We got jumped by ogres and minotaurs on our way here, that’s what happened! Their leader, Rumeon, demanded that we give over the goods immediately. We barely made it out alive.”

What bother! Things weren’t going in accordance with my plans. The gantry design I had come up with called for a great deal of construction materials, primarily metals, including rare alloying additives such as stalt and kergar, rare commodities on the market.

On my way back to my workshop I met one of the gunslingers I had hired to guard the place.

“Jangaard," I called out to him, "Know anything about a Rumeon? It seems he’s the bandit who's been robbing our merchants.”

The mercenary grinned.

“Damn right I know about him, but not from here. From back in Antagarich. That minotaur was a mercenary in service of Nighon during the war with Erathia, before switching over to Deyja.”

“Deyja, you say?”

I pondered. Some thought was bothering me.

“Never mind, though. Have you found out anything about the other minotaurs?”

“I've been watching those bandits lately. They seem to be crawling out of the old Dark Dwarf mines. I hear there's still a bunch of precious stuff to be had down there. Those were the minotaurs’ mines before the dwarves, but that was a long time ago... we weren't even in Jadame then.”

I lit a pipe and began thinking. Is there much iron ore left there? Maybe that's where we should look for the materials to build the gantry. I retired to my shop, pulled out the plans, and plunged deep into thought.

map.h4fact:4.header.description: The artificers Todd and Bertram vie to create the first Dreadnought. Todd's plan is to immediately use the engineering resources, while Bertram prioritizes economy. To win the scenario, outride your opponent. The level of heroes is unlimited.
map.h4fact:4.header.name: Deus Ex Machina
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.0.text: Ogres have sacked a trading post north of here. I wonder if there's anything left there?
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.1.text: Lately, I’ve been hearing more and more often about minotaurs raiding from the dungeons. How odd. Balthazar's minotaurs never attacked us. Perhaps these ones came from other lands?
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.2.text: I heard that one of the villages was attacked by ogres and minotaurs; but they have long been at war with each other. Why did they suddenly unite against us?
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.3.text: Gunslingers built their fort to the south.
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.4.text: Necromancers have started to appear here more frequently. It is said that they were expelled from the Guild after its new leaders came to power.
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.5.text: In the north, they say, a war has broken out between dragons and Erathian dragonslayers. And another pack of dragons has moved to our lands, too.
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.6.text: The dragons of Jadame are more unified than their relatives in other lands. They have built a mighty society in the mountains north of Ravage Roaming.
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.7.text: Warlocks and monsters have settled in the local caves, but right now it’s impossible to get rid of them completely.
map.h4fact:4.header.rumor.8.text: Every artificer dreams of creating machines like those from the Time of Wonders before the Silence. At least some of that dream now seems to be coming true.
map.h4fact:4.heroes.31.biography: Thulig is an extremely daring elf, and the best way to recruit him is to offer a challenge like "go I don't know where, bring I don't know what." He stole "don't-know-whats" from under a dragon's snout, an underground dwarven treasury, and even the mouth of an extinct volcano. High-profile failures are another trademark of his, and he has paid unequalled amounts in ransom for himself.
map.h4fact:4.heroes.31.name: Thulig
map.h4fact:4.heroes.46.biography: Lyadra's scope of interests covers any creatures capable of independent flight, especially those that look like they should not be flying at all, like bone dragons. Recently, she has also been drawn to the unusually rapid flight of angels; however, the scientific community is not yet prepared to accept Lyadra's theory that there is some kind of technology behind it.

map.h4fact:4.quest.1.13.1.completed:
You bring the Sleepkeeper up to the tower, and the stone tentacles start to twitch. It turns out that the whole tower is woven from them! You suddenly realize: as soon as you place the figurine in the opening, the tentacles will instantly retract into the ground and disappear forever.

Would you like to leave the Sleepkeeper here and go through?
map.h4fact:4.quest.1.13.1.firstVisit:
On the road stands a watchtower of an odd shape, made of some unknown material. All of a sudden, words start sounding right in your head:
"You who want to pass, open your mind. You who desire worldly goods, give up the protection the Sleeper’s likeness grants you. You who wish to prevail, know that everything carries a price.”
At the foot of the tower, a receptacle looking like the maw of some monster seems to have opened, framed by petrified tentacles. It appears as though you need to put an item in there.
map.h4fact:4.quest.1.13.1.nextVisit: The hole in the lower part of the tower still gapes greedily; you think you hear some kind of call, but it is completely unclear where it is coming from. So far, you are sure you don't have what you need to leave here.
map.h4fact:4.quest.1.66.0.completed: Will you accept a Gold dragon into your army, replacing a Green dragon?
map.h4fact:4.quest.1.66.0.firstVisit: Bring the young dragons to me, and one of my fellow gold dragons will join your cause.
map.h4fact:4.quest.1.66.0.nextVisit: Bring the young dragons to me, and one of my fellow gold dragons will join your cause.
map.h4fact:4.quest.10.13.1.completed:
The foreman of the tunnelers is schlepping a pair of work gloves made for the new employee; looks like he could easily wear either one for a raincoat.

Would you like to give the cyclops to the halflings and pass?
map.h4fact:4.quest.10.13.1.firstVisit:
You meet a crew of halflings with mining machinery, scratching their heads. The foreman in an oil-soaked coverall waves at you:

"Hey, buddy! We were sent here to clear a blockage in the tunnel, but we’ve run out of fuel. We can’t get our steamer going to push this rock off the road, but we still need to get the work done. Until we get a barrel or two of earth oil delivered, we could use a brawny helper. We've heard that there are some big guys in these parts who can handle heavy boulders like nobody’s business. Why don't you bring a lad like that to help us? Do a good deed, and you’ll be able to pass, too.”
map.h4fact:4.quest.10.13.1.nextVisit: The halflings are clattering and grinding their tools somewhere in the bowels of their malfunctioning steamer. There's no point in distracting them until you've found them a helper.
map.h4fact:4.quest.10.14.0.completed:
“So you say I can return to my cave now? Good news at last!” Rubbing his huge hands together contentedly, the Frost Giant invites you into the hut, where he treats you to some excellent Vori cheese, and then pulls a magical orb from his sack.

Would you like to accept the Orb of Firmament from the giant?
map.h4fact:4.quest.10.14.0.firstVisit:
As soon as we arrived at the doorstep of this strange, enormous hut, we felt a chill coming from inside. How odd...

Inside, it smelled of wool and cheese. We were greeted by an odd-looking bearded giant with bluish skin. At the sight of strangers, the giant grabbed his huge hammer, but as soon as he saw we were unarmed, he put it aside and got up from his table, as vast as a stage wandering minstrels perform on.

“Who are you, and which wind carried you here? You sure don't look like locals... Me, I'm stuck here, hundreds of miles away from my homeland! I suppose you've heard about our little war with Balthazar?”
I nodded silently.

“Of course you have. All of Jadame is gossiping about it these days. We came here from Vori in search of gold and booty. We struck an alliance with that minotaur; but then, our konung did a very foolish thing. He betrayed Balthazar and conspired with those vile creatures, the dark dwarves! The Minotaurs whupped our behinds good when they heard about it,” the Jotunn said, running his hand through his hair. “Some managed to fight their way to the ships and sail away, and I… I got stuck here. I wandered around for a while, found myself a cozy cave high up in the mountains; we Frost Giants love the cold. All would have been well, but then, the Titans showed up and chased me out of my new house!

Will you help me fight them? I can't handle them on my own, but you should be strong enough to do the job. If you do, I'll give you the magic orb we found during our quest.
map.h4fact:4.quest.10.14.0.nextVisit: “I know the titans are still in my cave. You better not come back to me with bad news!” roars the giant.
map.h4fact:4.quest.10.56.1.completed:
Canopus’ veil ripples and shimmers. It seems that its time is up; the spell holding it together is about to break, and you will be able to dispel it by simply waving your hand.

Do you wish to lift the veil and pass through?
map.h4fact:4.quest.10.56.1.firstVisit: The road is obstructed by an impenetrable magical veil. There are no signs of a deactivation mechanism—it appears designed to persist for some predetermined time before dissipating. This intricate enchantment is the creation of Canopus, a renowned wizard known for being a recluse. He trusts few and has not left his Bracadan castle in years. Who would have conjured this barrier? Perhaps Canopus found himself an apprentice or a kinsman who has now outshone his teacher?

As soon as the lab technician sees the bag of money, he brightens up and produces a bundle of tickets, beautifully printed on some bluish tanned leather.

Would you like to make the payment and proceed to the worm den?
map.h4fact:4.quest.2.29.0.firstVisit: Professor Agar, the new head of the Natural Science Department at the New Land Commonwealth Academic Board, has introduced a fee for visiting the sandworm habitat. He states that the fragile ecosystem these creatures inhabit requires careful protection and support, which comes at a significant cost. Those who pay the fee will also have the option to purchase a number of adult worms, a measure Agar claims is necessary to "regulate their population."
map.h4fact:4.quest.2.29.0.nextVisit: The lab technician put on duty here by the Academic Board refuses to let you pass without payment. For some reason, you are sure that you shouldn’t be messing with the man: those large worms crawling in the distance could pounce at you if they feel that you are mistreating their friend.

map.h4fact:4.quest.24.44.1.completed:
"Brought it? Get what we agreed on here, and I'll show you where to look!"

Give the shady character the fee for showing you the way to the secret?
map.h4fact:4.quest.24.44.1.firstVisit:
In a small cave, you come across a suspicious character, hiding some stuff among the rocks.
"Hey, don't you touch me! I'm not up to any shenanigans here. And if you kill me, you won't know the secret.”
“What secret?"
"Sir Mullich's own secret! If you wish, I'll tell you where I hid it, but you’ll have to pay me!”
map.h4fact:4.quest.24.44.1.nextVisit: The rascal flinches at the sight of you, but remains adamant: he still demands a hefty fee for Sir Mullich's secret.
map.h4fact:4.quest.26.48.0.completed: Do you wish to restore the Halfling Adobe?
map.h4fact:4.quest.26.48.0.firstVisit: The halfling adobe lies in ruins after a raid by the ogres from the wastelands. The halflings seek your help: it will take 10 wood and 5000 gold to rebuild their huts.
map.h4fact:4.quest.26.48.0.nextVisit: The halfling adobe lies in ruins after a raid by the ogres from the wastelands. The halflings seek your help: it will take 10 wood and 5000 gold to rebuild their huts.
map.h4fact:4.quest.3.35.0.completed:
“I can't do this anymore! Take it, take it away from me! Put the gems over there, grab the figurine, and leave! I don't recall the last time I slept..." the ragged man cries out. Apparently, the thing failed to prevent his stress-induced mental collapse, but if it is indeed capable of blocking insidious mind magic directed from the outside, it could serve a valuable purpose.

Would you like to trade the valuables for the Sleepkeeper?
map.h4fact:4.quest.3.35.0.firstVisit:
In the hut, you meet a ragamuffin suffering from a severe nervous tic. His eyes are wide, his lips move soundlessly and his eyelids flutter, and it's only after a couple of minutes that he finally speaks.

"Thank gods, some ordinary people... dwarves... I don't care who—at least you’re no otherworldly creatures with tentacles all over their mugs! Want to hear how I ended up like this? Well, here goes. A while ago, my brother and I took some coin we’d saved up and decided to invest it to turn some profit. What possessed us to get involved with that stranger in the tavern, I’ll never know. He sweet-talked us, claiming he knew about an ancient crypt brimming with artifacts—the kind that Burtonese artifices are after. He sold us a map and some golden trinket, assuring us we wouldn't have to worry about the spirits guarding the place.

Well, we did find the crypt and even got inside, and right away we saw some dark creatures there. At first we stood and laughed as they attempted to work some magic on us... then they realized it wasn't doing any good, and came at us! You know what? I've never heard of spirits with knuckles like that! One grabbed me by the scruff and gave me a hell of a thrashing, then threw me out. The other one came out after me, with my brother dangling in his paws like a toy. The thing grabbed his head with its tentacles and tore it clean off! I ran for the hills, of course, and I've been hiding in this hole for months now, shaking at every noise, expecting the freaks to pay me a return visit.

Listen, could you take this golden bauble off my hands? It does protect against magicks, but I’m scared to even glance at it now. I won’t ask for much in return, surely far less than we paid for this ill-fated adventure."
map.h4fact:4.quest.3.35.0.nextVisit: Entering the hut, you're met with an odd sight: the ragamuffin sits on the floor, unblinkingly staring at the figurine of an enigmatic creature before him. He appears to be trying to look away, but an unseen force repeatedly draws his gaze back. For now, you cannot pay him to take it off his hands—he must endure the presence of this peculiar idol for a while longer.
map.h4fact:4.quest.31.12.0.completed:
The pass office potentate, with a deferential expression, issues the permit in elegant handwriting and personally guides you to the gate.

Would you like to pass?
map.h4fact:4.quest.31.12.0.firstVisit:
Gunslingers armed with the latest masterpieces of Burtonese armories stand guard at the gate. However, the most powerful weapon on this outpost is hardly a gun. It sits on the forehead of a runty character wearing black sleeve protectors, who occupies a booth designated as "Pass Office," sorting through some papers. This formidable object is a special-purpose magic eyepiece, designed to detect forged seals and signatures with unerring accuracy.

"Passes are granted only to those who possess original documents verifying a long-term employment contract with the council of a New Land Commonwealth town," the bureaucrat announces tonelessly. These documents serve as proof of citizenship around here. Evidently, the right of passage is limited to reputable artificers and mercenaries who have completed all necessary paperwork and undergone the required procedures.
map.h4fact:4.quest.31.12.0.nextVisit:
The little man in the booth glances briefly at your documents and shoves them away in disgust, without even bothering to look through his eyepiece.
“Did you truly expect to fool me with such sloppy forgery? I could take offense and summon the guards... but you're fortunate I really cannot be bothered. Get out, you two-bit card-sharper!”
map.h4fact:4.quest.33.28.1.completed:
"One-eyed grunts, huh? Well, that's no big deal—I’ve taught one-legged men to goose-step just fine. But they’re built just right, aren’t they! Come on, boys, hep-two!” the old man exclaims contentedly and waves you over.

Would you like to proceed and train your troops?
map.h4fact:4.quest.33.28.1.firstVisit: An elderly retired commander resides here. Once a figure of great renown, he penned many influential treatises on training new soldiers. Recently, three of his trusted batmen have succumbed to old age one after another, leaving him bereft. The commander is, however, still fairly spry and seeks new men to fill their roles. Preferring stalwart and imposing figures, he envisions them as formidable right-flank men. If you bring him suitable candidates, he will be willing to drill your troops—for a fair compensation, that is.
map.h4fact:4.quest.33.28.1.nextVisit: The old general snores loudly in a chair on the porch of his house, occasionally barking orders through his sleep. You are loath to disturb the man until you have something to please him with.
map.h4fact:4.quest.33.46.1.firstVisit:
A grim guard at the gate hums lifelessly from the depths of his kettle-like helmet:
"Password is required to enter Castle Lincoln."
You have no idea what kind of password is needed here, and the name of the castle does not give you any ideas. It doesn’t look like you can get through here.
map.h4fact:4.quest.33.46.1.nextVisit:

"Password is required to enter Castle Lincoln."
You have no idea what kind of password is needed here, and the name of the castle does not give you any ideas. It doesn’t look like you can get through here.
map.h4fact:4.quest.33.5.0.completed:
The artificer is pleased to meet someone who could trial his creations.

Would you like to receive prototypes of improved arms?
map.h4fact:4.quest.33.5.0.firstVisit: In this experimental workshop, drills squeal and grinding stones screech: work is underway here to improve all kinds of arms.  The artificer who manages the shop agrees to provide you with some prototypes, but only if you prove that you are experienced enough to not damage them with clumsy handling.
map.h4fact:4.quest.33.5.0.nextVisit: The artificer asks you to take a few tests; however, after browsing the first filled out page, he crumples the papers and throws them away indignantly. So far, you haven't managed to convince him that you're trustworthy.
map.h4fact:4.quest.34.37.0.firstVisit:
Agreement.

We, the undersigned, Bertram Hard Word, son of Bolton Silver Belly, son of Benoit Deep Pocket [11 lines omitted] of the Twice-Belted Goldsmiths Clan of Mount Lesser Smoked Head (hereinafter referred to as "Bertram"), and Todd (hereinafter referred to as "Todd"), covenant that until either of us has built a prototype weapon, the specifications for which are set forth in Appendix 15.6 to this Agreement, we shall not cross the boundaries of each other's laboratory compounds by any means, including but not limited to foot, horse, air, or magic (the respective territories shall be delineated in accordance with Section 7.12 of this Agreement). The above likewise applies to our Allies, hereafter referred to as "Spies."

The violator shall be shamed and get the lash.

Todd

Bertram

map.h4fact:4.quest.49.40.0.completed: Do you wish to rebuild the Foundry?
map.h4fact:4.quest.49.40.0.firstVisit: Todd's foundry took severe damage in a fire. The mechanics ask for 10 wood and 5000 gold to rebuild the destroyed structure.
map.h4fact:4.quest.49.40.0.nextVisit: Todd's foundry took severe damage in a fire. The mechanics ask for 10 wood and 5000 gold to rebuild the destroyed structure.
map.h4fact:4.quest.5.6.0.completed:
After learning that Tharud will no longer misappropriate the values obtained through their hard, hazardous work, the miners agree to share some of the crystals with you in gratitude.

Would you like to proceed to the cave?
map.h4fact:4.quest.5.6.0.firstVisit: The miners who extract rock crystal and other valuable things here have built an outpost and won't let anyone near their cave. Their foreman insists this is out of dire necessity: the warlock Tharud and his gang have already come here several times to rob them blind. You have heard rumors about this eccentric character: he sells enchanted spectacles, which, per his claims, should restore anyone’s eyesight to perfection. You haven’t the slightest idea how a troglodyte is able to convince anyone of his expertise in optometry, and even low-key admire his audacity, but one thing is clear: you will have to find him and teach him a lesson in honest dealings in order to win over the miners and profit from their labor.
map.h4fact:4.quest.5.6.0.nextVisit: The miners are confident that Tharud is still a threat to their peace of mind; once again, they’d seen his henchmen nosing around near the cave. You'd better find that scoundrel soon.
